records.title: Who is doing this, and on whose money
records.summary: Who runs Olive Branch
records.text: About this chapter | Olive Branch | ExposeMississippi Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Olive Branch, MS of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → About · Olive Branch, MS Who is doing this, and on whose money This is the Olive Branch chapter of the Move Weight Foundation , a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. It is independent of the City of Olive Branch, of DeSoto County, and of the State of Mississippi. It takes no money from any of them. How we source claims Every factual claim on this site links to a primary document or to a named outlet. Where a document exists, we publish the document rather than our description of it. We never invent a government phone number, address or docket number. Every contact datum is transcribed from an official published source and dated on the page. If we have not transcribed it yet, the page says so and links to the city's own directory instead of guessing. Every external link is fetched before it is published , and re-checked automatically every week. The result of that check is public on the automation page . Sources for this chapter were last verified 2026-07-26 . We publish released records whole. No redaction of a public record the government has already released. We never allege a crime. We publish the document, the amount and the date, and let readers and prosecutors do their own jobs. A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in file metadata. We link out to local news and never republish it. What this chapter is not It is not a newspaper, not a campaign, and not aligned with any candidate, party or slate. It does not endorse. Its output is records, an archive, and the plain fact of whether a public body answered a lawful request on time. Funding The Foundation is funded by individual donations. Records cost money — Mississippi allows a body to charge for search and copying under § 25-61-7, and a single large request can run into real numbers. Donations pay those invoices, the servers that hold the archive, and nothing else. Contributions are tax-deductible. Zelle: team@moveweight.com . Financial disclosures and the Form 990 are published by the Foundation at foundation.moveweight.com . Corrections If something here is wrong, we want to fix it and we will say that we did. Send the correction and, if you have it, the document — here . A correction is never quietly edited in; the change and its date stay on the page. Contact Records and requests: foia@moveweight.com Everything else: expose@moveweight.net

records.summary: When every automated pull for this chapter last ran, whether it succeeded, and what is out of date right now. Published whether it is flattering or not.

This page reports what actually happened, including when it failed. A site that quietly rots looks identical to one that is current, right up until somebody relies on it. So the status below is generated by the jobs themselves — it is not maintained by hand and cannot be made to look better than it is. Status Loading the last run… Job What it does Last run Result Detail Loading… What each job is allowed to do Agendas and meetings. Fetches only documents Olive Branch has already published, from CivicPlus AgendaCenter at https://www.obms.us/AgendaCenter . It never logs in, never submits anything, and never touches a page the city has not made public. Link check. Re-fetches every external link this chapter publishes. Cities move pages, and a records-request link that 404s fails a reader at the exact moment they were about to act. Search index. Rebuilds the site's index from the pages and the extracted agenda text, so a resident can search a phrase and land on the agenda that carried it. Nothing writes to a government system. Records requests are sent by a person, deliberately, never by a timer. If a job has been red for a while That is a bug, not a policy. Tell us — the whole point of publishing this page is that somebody outside the project can see the failure before we do.

records.title: Every official link, in one place
records.summary: Verified links to Olive Branch city government, DeSoto County offices, records portals, budgets and Mississippi oversight bodies. Checked 2026-07-26.
records.text: Olive Branch City Desk — every official link in one place | Olive Branch | ExposeMississippi Skip to content Records & transparency Public records request form The City's own PDF request form. https://www.obms.us/DocumentCenter/View/768/PUBLIC-RECORDS-REQUEST-FORM Document Center https://www.obms.us/DocumentCenter County & state DeSoto County https://www.desotocountyms.gov/ Mississippi Ethics Commission A records denial appeals here free. https://www.ethics.state.ms.us/ Mississippi Office of the State Auditor https://www.osa.ms.gov/ Mississippi oversight Where a Olive Branch decision gets reviewed by somebody who does not work for Olive Branch. Mississippi Ethics Commission A denial appeals here FREE under § 25-61-13. The Commission can order release and fine the official who wrongfully withheld. This is the strongest citizen remedy of the three states. Mississippi Office of the State Auditor Audits municipalities and counties; published reports are public records. Meetings, and how to be in the room Olive Branch publishes its agendas through CivicPlus AgendaCenter : https://www.obms.us/AgendaCenter Agendas are posted ahead of the meeting because the law requires it. That posting is the single most useful document in local government and almost nobody opens it — it is where a contract award, a rate change or a tax abatement appears in public for the first time, usually as one line in a consent agenda. Reading a consent agenda Items on a consent agenda are voted through together, with no discussion, in a few seconds. That is not a trick — it is how a body gets through routine business. But it means the only chance to see an item is before the meeting, in the packet. Any member can pull an item out for discussion, and so can a resident who asks one in time. Where to watch → Open the agenda portal → A link that does not work Cities move pages. Every link on this page is re-checked automatically each week and the result is published on the automation page . If one is broken and we have not caught it, tell us .

records.title: Read the people who cover this every day
records.summary: Local and statewide newsrooms covering Olive Branch and Mississippi. We link out; we never republish another newsroom
records.text: Olive Branch news & allies | Olive Branch | ExposeMississippi Skip to content Why we link instead of republish Local newsrooms are paid by attention. An aggregator that lifts a paragraph and keeps the reader on its own page takes that attention and gives nothing back, and then the newsroom shrinks and there is less reporting for everyone — including for us, because most of what a records request confirms was first noticed by a reporter. So the rule here is absolute: link out, never republish . The only documents hosted on this site are public records, which belong to the public already. Working on Olive Branch? If you are a reporter, a nonprofit or a resident group working on something here, the archive and the request pipeline are yours to use, and we will file on your behalf if a request under your own name would cost you something. Get in touch .

records.title: File a request the city has to answer
records.summary: How to file a public records request with the City of Olive Branch under Miss. Code Ann. § 25-61-1 et seq. — the deadline, the fees, the appeal, and a letter you can copy.
records.text: File a Mississippi Public Records Act request in Olive Branch | Olive Branch | ExposeMississippi Skip to content Build your letter This runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type here is sent anywhere, stored, or seen by us — copy the result and send it yourself from your own email. Your name Your email What you are asking for Date range Ask for electronic delivery Require a cost estimate before charges Require an itemised legal basis for anything withheld Copy the letter Write the request narrow, then widen it “All emails about the project” gets refused as overbroad and burns your deadline. “Emails between the City Manager and [named party] between 1 March and 30 April” gets answered. Once you see what came back, ask again with what you learned. Two narrow requests beat one that never gets filled. Where to send it Olive Branch's own records channel is listed on the City Desk , with the exact URL the City publishes. Use it — a request filed through the body's own portal is the hardest one for it to say it never received. Send a copy to foia@moveweight.com at the same time. We log the send date, watch the deadline, and if it lapses we publish that fact. A request nobody knows about is a request the city can ignore quietly. Track the clock § 25-61-5 gives the City seven (7) working days. Put the send date in your calendar with that many days added, and put a second reminder a week later. Most requests are not denied — they are simply never answered, and the only thing that changes that is somebody noticing on the exact day. If you are refused A denial appeals free to the Mississippi Ethics Commission under § 25-61-13. The Commission can order the record released and impose a civil penalty on the official who wrongfully withheld it. This is the strongest citizen remedy of the three states this Foundation works in, and almost nobody uses it. Keep the refusal Whatever the outcome, keep the exact wording of the denial and the date. A refusal that cites no statute, or cites one that does not apply, is itself the story — and it is the document an appeal turns on.

records.title: The other side of the DeSoto County tax base
records.summary: The structural question this chapter was opened on, the specific public record that answers it, and what has been asked for so far.
records.text: What we are asking Olive Branch | Olive Branch | ExposeMississippi Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Olive Branch, MS of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → The Question · Olive Branch, MS The other side of the DeSoto County tax base Olive Branch shares a county, a tax base, a water table and an industrial corridor with Southaven — where an ad valorem tax agreement abating two thirds of property tax on a recital of twenty new jobs is already published in full on this Foundation's Mississippi chapter. The same agreements, the same aquifer and the same board structure exist here, and no one has asked for them. This is a question, not an accusation No one at this Foundation has alleged that anybody in Olive Branch has done anything wrong, and nothing on this site should be read that way. Chapters are opened on structural risk — large capital programmes, fast growth, a single dominant employer, a utility or authority that meets away from the council — because those are the conditions under which decisions get made with nobody watching. That is a statement about attention, not about anybody's conduct. Naming a city next to an accusation we have not documented would be precisely the thing this project exists to oppose. So the page you are reading names the question and the record that settles it, and then we go and ask for the record. The record that answers it Ad valorem tax exemption agreements approved by the Board of Aldermen, and the City's water-well permits and monthly pumpage reports. How this gets resolved Ask. A request goes to the City of Olive Branch under Miss. Code Ann. § 25-61-1 et seq.. The City has seven (7) working days. Publish what comes back, whole. Released public records go up unredacted. We do not summarise a document in place of showing it, and we do not redact what the government already released. Publish what does not come back. A missed deadline, a refusal with no statute cited, an estimate that prices a resident out — those get published too, with dates. Silence is a finding. Rewrite this page. When the documents are in, this page stops being a question and becomes what the records showed — including if they showed nothing. A chapter that only ever reports wrongdoing is not doing arithmetic, it is doing marketing. What you can do right now You do not need us. The statute is yours, and a request from a resident of Olive Branch is harder to wave away than one from a nonprofit two states over. Build the letter → Where to send it → Send us something anonymously →

records.title: Watch your government
records.summary: Where to watch Olive Branch government on video — meeting recordings, agendas, and the archives that keep them after the city takes them down.
records.text: Watch your government | Olive Branch | ExposeMississippi Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Olive Branch, MS of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Video · Olive Branch, MS Watch your government Almost every decision that costs you money is made in a room with a camera in it. The recordings are public. Most people never find them because they are buried three clicks deep on a government site. Here they are. Where the video lives These are Olive Branch's own recordings and portals. We link to them rather than rehosting, so you are watching the authoritative copy. City of Olive Branch on Facebook City of Olive Branch The City's own page, linked from obms.us. Olive Branch does not publish a YouTube archive — which is itself the gap this chapter documents. Open → We link, we do not rehost These are the government's own recordings on the government's own platforms. We send you there rather than mirroring them, so you are watching the authoritative copy and the view count lands where it belongs. The exception is when a recording disappears — see below. When a recording goes missing Meeting video gets taken down. Sometimes it is a retention policy, sometimes a platform migration, sometimes nobody can say why. Either way the public record evaporates, and the one meeting you needed is the one that is gone. That is why the Foundation's Miami, Oklahoma chapter keeps 522 meetings archived with machine transcripts and captions , mirrored to the Internet Archive. It is the deepest archive we run and the model for every other chapter. See what a full archive looks like → If you spot a gap A meeting with no video, a recording that ends mid-item, a link that used to work — tell us . A missing recording is itself a records request: the city holds the raw file whether or not it publishes it, and we will ask for it. Getting more out of a meeting recording Read the agenda packet first. It usually contains the actual contract or ordinance. The video is people discussing a document you can already have in front of you. Note the timestamp of anything that matters. A citation like "14 January, 1:42:10" is something a reporter or an auditor can verify in a minute. Watch the vote, not the speech. Who moved it, who seconded, who was absent, and whether it was on a published agenda. Executive session is a flag, not a crime. Bodies may close a meeting for defined reasons and must certify which. If a payment or a contract was discussed behind a closed door, the certification is a public record. Ask for it → Follow this chapter No social accounts yet for this chapter. We publish to the site first. Social accounts are a distribution channel, never the record — anything we post there exists here with its source document attached.

records.summary: Page 1 of 10 MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT REGULAR MEETING JUNE 11, 2026 The Olive Branch Board of Adjustment meeting was held on Thursday, June 11, 2026, in the Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m. CALL TO ORDER The meeting was called to order by Mr. Roman, Chairman of Board of Zoning Adjustment, at 6:00 p.m. ROLL CALL Darrel Berk
records.text:
Page 1 of 10
 MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT
REGULAR MEETING JUNE 11, 2026
The Olive Branch Board of Adjustment meeting was held on Thursday, June 11, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Roman, Chairman of Board of Zoning Adjustment, at 
6:00 p.m. 
ROLL CALL
Darrel Berkley, William Gray, Aretha Wiseman, Jackie Butler, Ted Roman, and Carl Williams were
present, and a quorum was established. McKeever Heun was absent. Venard Asongayi, Director,
Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, and Heather James,
Planning Technician, were present from the Planning and Development Department.
THE APPEAL PROCESS
Mr. Roman announced the Appeal Process.
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE MAY 14, 2026 MEETING
Mr. Roman asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the May
14, 2026 meeting. Carl Williams made a motion to approve the minutes. William Gray made the
second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Yes Carl Williams – Yes
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
1.
Application for a Design Variance, submitted by Greg Smith, Civil-Link, on behalf of
property owner, Harvest Church of Desoto. The request is for a temporary use of CR
610 limestone surface in lieu of asphalt or concrete for parking area expansion. The
5.3+/-acre subject property is zoned A-R, Agricultural-Residential District, and is
located at the northeast corner of Old Goodman Rd and Polk Lane, known as 12050
Old Goodman Rd. (File # VR-26-0003).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
The applicant, Greg Smith of Civil-Link, on behalf of the property owner, Harvest
Church of Desoto, requests approval of a Design Variance to allow the temporary use of a
CR 610 limestone aggregate surface in lieu of the required asphalt or concrete paving for an
expansion of the church parking area located at 12050 Old Goodman Road. The church
proposes to expand its existing parking facilities better accommodate attendance associated
with scheduled worship services and periodic church events. The proposed improvements
include grading and preparation of the full parking area and all required parking spaces, with
the aggregate surface as an interim parking treatment for a period of 2 years.

Page 2 of 10

STAFF PRESENTATION
Associate Planner, Jeremiah McCroskey, presented the staff report, which is
included herein by reference (File # VR-26-0003).

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None

PUBLIC HEARING
o
Proponents:

Greg Smith, Civil-Link, 5779 Getwell, Southaven, MS – He said this is a 
temporary solution. They are asking to only pave the first 65 feet of the 
driveway as that is a more logical space to end the paving since it’s at the
curve. 

Michael Hatcher, 12841 Old Country Cove, Olive Branch, MS – he said 
the church has grown in membership and outgrown the parking lot. They 
now average 120 members on Sunday mornings. They are asking the 
100 feet of paving be reduced to 65 feet. It’s a growing church and they 
have to be conscious of the budget.
o
Opponents:

None

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
Mrs. Butler asked what the difference in cost between paving 65 feet vs 100 feet.
Mr. Hatcher hasn’t gotten numbers yet because they were waiting on the outcome of this
meeting before sending out for bids. He said that 2 years would give them time to study 
the growth and see if anything else needs to be added. Mr. Roman asked how soon 
after the gravel is done would they work on asphalt. Mr. Hatcher said they are studying 
everything now and may have to add extra buildings because of the growth. They don’t 
want to ruin asphalt now with construction traffic. Mr. Williams is concerned about the 
gravel dragout onto the road. The standard of paving 100 feet is to keep the gravel from
entering the highway from the driveway. Mrs. Butler said that the residents around the 
church would have to deal with the gravel in the road. Mrs. Butler asked staff if 65 feet 
was a reasonable alternative. Mr. McCroskey advised that 100 is standard practice. Mr.
Roman asked to clarify the plan would be to pave driveway, gravel the lot, deal with 
drainage issue, then come back for any future requests. Mr. Hatcher said the water 
issue comes from under the property. Ms. Wiseman said that if 100 feet is the standard,
we don’t need to change that standard to set a precedent for future requests. 

MOTION
Mrs. Butler made a motion, based upon a positive finding by the Board of
Adjustment that all conditions have been met, to approve the requested Design
Variance to allow a temporary CR 610 limestone parking surface in lieu of asphalt
or concrete paving, for a period of 2 years, non-renewable subject to the following
conditions:
1.
All site improvements shall be the responsibility of the developer, and not
the City of Olive Branch.
2.
The approval shall apply only to the temporary use of a CR 610 limestone
aggregate surface for the proposed parking expansion. 
3.
The parking area shall be properly graded and maintained to control dust,
erosion, and drainage impacts. 

Page 3 of 10
4.
Any future paving or expansion activities shall be approved by the City
Engineer
with
all
applicable
site
plan,
drainage,
and
development
requirements in effect at the time of construction. 
5.
The variance approval shall not waive any other applicable federal, state,
or local regulations.
6.
The first 100 ft of the driveway from Old Polk Lane must be paved before
the proposed limestone surface may be used for parking.
7.
The parking area must be paved before June 11, 2028.
Mr. Gray made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Yes Carl Williams – Yes
2.
Application for a Zoning Variance, submitted by Robert Pryor, property owner. The
request is to encroach 30 feet into the 50-foot front setback to install a privacy fence
at this location.
The 0.90+/-acre subject property is zoned PUD, Planned Unit
Development, and is located at the northwest corner of Summer Pointe Dr and Malone
Rd N, known as 3990 Summer Pointe Dr. (File # VR-26-0004).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
The subject property is a corner lot with front yards on both Malone Rd and Summer
Pointe Dr. As such, the provision of Art. VII, Sec. 2(B)(1)(c)(ii)(A) of the Zoning Ordinance
that “No fence, wall, or hedge shall be erected, constructed or maintained within the required

MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH PLANNING COMMISSION
REGULAR MEETING JUNE 9, 2026
The Olive Branch Planning Commission meeting was held on Tuesday, June 9, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Dorr, Chairman of Planning Commission, at 6:00 p.m. 
He announced he would be retiring at the end of this month and this would be his last meeting.
ROLL CALL
Janice Lewis, Dion Jones, Diane Senger, Pat Dorr, Steve Stratton and Mark Long were present,
and a quorum was established. Donny Singh was absent. Venard Asongayi, Director, Kevin 
Norman, Senior Planner, Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, and Heather James, 
Planning Technician, were present from the Planning and Development Department. 
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE MAY 12, 2026 MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the May
12, 2026 meeting. Mr. Jones made a motion to approve the minutes as presented. Mr. Stratton
made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Yes Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
CONSENT AGENDA
OLD BUSINESS
1.
Consideration of an application for the Final Plat of Center Hill Farms, Phase 2, submitted by
Alex Gagne, M&R Builders, on behalf of property owner, Johnny McBride. The request is to
create 62 single-family residential lots and 6 common open spaces from 23.78+/-acres. The
subject property is zoned PUD, Planned Unit Development District, and is located on the
west side of Center Hill Rd, beginning at the north end of Lucy Drive. (File #SD-26-0006).
(Tabled to this date at meeting of May 12, 2026).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Alexander Gagne, on behalf of Johnny McBride, member, Center Hill Development, LLC,
property owner, requests that the Planning Commission table to its July 14, 2026 meeting,
the consideration of the final plat for Center Hill Farms Subdivision, Phase II. While
subdivision infrastructure construction is ongoing, it is not yet sufficiently completed for final
plat approval. The first lift of asphalt, for example, has not yet been laid on proposed public
streets. Also, some utility lines are still to be installed: their construction may warrant the
establishment of utility easements and associated adjustment of lot lines to create sufficient
buildable areas on proposed lots.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, presented the staff report, which is included
herein by reference (File # SD-26-0006).

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None


PUBLIC MEETING

public hearing was required for a plat application.
o
Proponents:


o
Opponents:

None

PLANNING COMMISISON DISCUSSION
None

MOTION
Mr. Jones made a motion to approve the final plat for Phase 2 of Center Hill Farms
Planned Residential Development and recommend same to the Board of Aldermen
subject to the following: 
1.
Improvements shall be the responsibility of the developer and not the 
responsibility of the City of Olive Branch. 
2.
All utilities and services (electric, telephone, cable, etc) shall be 
installed underground. The water service lines shall be installed with 
tracing wire at the top.
3.
All approval conditions of the preliminary plat are maintained.
4.
The developer shall submit to the City of Olive Branch a letter of credit 
of sufficient amount as will be determined by the City Engineer, plus a 
25% contingency, for the completion of all uncompleted public 
improvements required in the land area constitutive of the final plat and 
for any outstanding As-Built drawings before recordation of the final 
plat.
5.
A building permit shall not be issued for construction on the proposed 
lots until the first lift of asphalt has been laid on all streets or street 
sections included in this final plat of Phase 2 of Center Hill Farms 
Subdivision. 
6.
Minor edits may be applicable to the subdivision plat as may be 
determined necessary by the City Engineer and the Director of Planning
and Development or their designees.
7.
The final plat for Center Hill Farms Phase II shall not be recorded until 
the first lift of asphalt has been installed on all streets included in this 
phase of the subdivision. 
8.
Minor edits may be applicable to the subdivision plat as may be 
determined necessary by the City Engineer and the Director of Planning
and Development or their designees.
Mr. Singh made the second and the motion was approved as follows:

Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes

Consideration of an application for a Zoning Map Amendment, submitted by Bob Barber,
Orion Planning Design, on behalf of property owners R. R. Bridgforth Heirs, Bettye B
Funderburk, Etal, and Dudley B. Bridgforth Jr, Etal. The request is to rezone 561.8+/-acres
from A, Agricultural District and A-R, Agricultural-Residential District to M-3, Planned
Industrial District for the purpose of creating the Desoto Innovation District.
The subject
property is located within the northwest corner of Church Road and Craft Rd. (File # RZN-26-
0002).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Bob Barber, Orion Planning Design, on behalf of property owners R. R. Bridgforth Heirs,
Bettye B Funderburk, Etal, and Dudley B. Bridgforth Jr, Etal. request to rezone 561.8+/-acres
from A, Agricultural Residential, and A-R, Agricultural-Residential District to M-3, Planned
Industrial District for the purpose of creating the Desoto Innovation District, which will consist
of three principal areas: a ±141ac Cleanfill Area for rubbish disposal; a ±336ac area for light
manufacturing and technology oriented uses; and ±85ac of surrounding natural buffer. Heavy
duty trucks (18-wheelers) access would be restricted to Nail Rd extension unto Hwy 305.
The current Cleanfill site has attained full capacity and needs to be decommissioned. The
Planning Commission may recommend approval of the rezoning request and associated
preliminary development plan (subject to various conditions) upon finding that the character
of the area has historically been industrial and that there is a public need for a cost effective
new Cleanfill site inside the City of Olive Branch and for industrial land to provide for more
employment opportunities within the City limits. Alternatively, a denial recommendation may
be rendered upon finding that the character of the area west of Craft Rd and north of Church
Rd has changed from industrial to predominantly agricultural and residential in the last twenty
five years, which the proposed rezoning is misaligned with, and that the Future Land Use
Map in the Comprehensive Plan 2040 designates most of the subject property as “Rural
Estate” (for residential use).

STAFF PRESENTATION
Venard Asongayi, Director, presented the staff report, which is included herein by
reference (File # RZN-26-0002). He advised at the end of the presentation, there would be
two separate motions: one for the rezoning action and the other for the recommendation for
the project text.

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
Mr. Jones asked to clarify the Comp Plan stated both that the landfill area would be used
as recreational, but also planned use was industrial for the same area.

PUBLIC HEARING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone was present to speak for the application.
o
Proponents:


Bob Barber, 919 Getwell Rd S, Hernando, MS – he provided an additional
presentation and advised if the rezoning was not approved, which 
included the landfill expansion, there would be an increase in costs to the 
cities for disposing of this excess. He stated there have been 12 changes
in the vicinity, leading to a change in the area.

Jesse Medlin, County Supervisor, Hernando, MS – he advised the 
rubbish pit belongs to the people but is operated by the county. They 
normally would use old gravel pits for these and the same goes for this 
location. This will only hold limbs and building materials, not any 
household garbage. The rubbish is picked up currently by the same 
place in Marshall County that we will have to send everything to if this is 
not approved. It currently costs over $300,000 this year alone. The 
current landfill has been there for over 40 years and is almost full. It will 
take about 1-1.5 years to obtain permits if this is approved.

Jim McNaughton, Environmental Business Services – he advised the 
current landfill is about a year out from having to be closed down.

Billy Klauser, Desoto Council, 4716 Pepperchase Dr, Southaven, MS – 
he said that healthcare research, manufacturing research & development 
are all under advanced manufacturing and that’s what they are looking to 
add to this development. 
o
Opponents:

Ted Roman, 4711 W Sandidge, Olive Branch, MS – he said there has 
been a change in character from 1966 to 2026, but the major changes 
have been residential and commercial, not industrial. Residential and 
commercial growth all support the neighborhoods. It’s a huge jump to ask
for rezoning to M3 and it will be a major impact. The only public need is 
the rubbish pit. The Comp Plan of 2022 mentioned this was coming in 
the future. The county has had years to plan for this and should find 
somewhere else. There is tons of trash everywhere already. The City 
tries to keep it up, but that’s the City trying to maintain it, not the County. 
This doesn’t fit with the Comp Plan. This area is designated as green 
space/park area. 

Scott Dauberger, 4825 Cherry Tree, Olive Branch, MS – he lives 
downstream and his house is in the flood zone. The creeks are full now, 
and the existing ponds are not holding water, so it floods already. He’s 
concerned eminent domain will be enacted and just take the land for the 
landfill.

Ramiro Gonzalez, 4535 Plantation Garden Dr, Olive Branch, MS – his 
concern is that in option 1 for approval, where the improvements are the 
responsibility of the developer, it assumes a lot of trust that developers 
will do what they should. He prefers option 2 to deny. 

Ricky Denton, 6280 Northwood Dr, Olive Branch, MS – his property 
backs up to Church Rd. When Church Rd expanded, it destroyed the 
quiet area and they don’t want anything else. If the landfill issue is the 

primary issue with this, why wasn’t it addressed before now. He has 
concerns with the buffer and other questions in writing that he wants to 
submit. Will the buffer include the existing mature tree line. They need 
the buffer to be enough. What is the elevation going to be like? Will this 
all be leveled out. They don’t want to hear, see or smell it. We live here 
like the developers, but we don’t have the resources they do.

Chris Turnbow, 9552 Miranda Dr, Olive Branch, MS – said this plan is for 
up to 14 lots and he said there was another concept A for 2 lots. Has that 
plan gone away? Just because they have taken data centers off the table 
for today, does that mean it won’t be brought back later? Have they done
power studies? The all or nothing plan is a problem.

Donna McBride, 6401 Spring Creek Dr, Olive Branch, MS – they have 
lived in Pleasant Hill Estates since 2002. The classification is M3, 
allowing heavy manufacturing including hazardous materials. If that is the
case, they have a concern. 

Pam Bean, 10160 Quail Rd, Olive Branch, MS – she wants to keep as 
much agricultural land as possible. According to the Comp Plan of 2022, 
there was only 10% left. She said it should be used for recycling and 
teaching, as a way to keep things out of the landfill. She sited a 
company, McNeil Station, that recycles to produce energy. This needs to 
be taught here. There will be an impact from the sound of industrial use. 
If trash is a problem, look to find other solutions. 

Keith Rubrum, 4822 Stone Cross Dr, Olive Branch, MS – what is 
innovative manufacturing? What does that mean? What pollution will this
produce? How will this affect water and power bills?

Ashley Bishop, 9678 Stuart Cv, Olive Branch, MS – recycling the 
materials that go into the landfill would be a better use. There are 
already traffic issues and warehouses will cause this to be worse.

Joe Crawford, 4693 E Dublin Cir, Olive Branch, MS – he said the problem
we are in is because of a lack of trust in government. He was asked if he 
had anything to say about this rezoning application and to stay on topic. 
He offered nothing else about the application. 

Brenda Brown, 7268 Old South Dr, Olive Branch, MS – she wanted to 
know if there would be a requirement for a groundwater study.

Sunnie Barkley, 6460 Northwood Cove, Olive Branch, MS – there is 
already noise and we can’t hear a conversation in our back yard as it is. 
Who polices the development once it’s built. How many cars do they 
expect on the employee road. This will exit onto Church Rd and the 
neighbors will be disturbed by lights day and night. We want a berm 
along Pleasant Hill Estates if this is approved.


Mike Briggs, 9314 Austin Dr, Olive Branch, MS – eventually this will be 
Industrial and not on Church Rd. this will force us to have more heavy 
trucks on Church Rd and it’s not built for that.

Michael Sheid, 6303 Darren Dr, Olive Branch, MS – trucks turn around all
the time and they already aren’t allowed. This will be worse. There is no 
plan to connect the walking trail to the existing one on Craft Rd.

PLANNING COMMISISON DISCUSSION
Mrs. Lewis asked when this would need to be shut down and Mr. McNaughton advised a
year. She asked if the applicant would consider pulling the landfill portion out of this 
application and submitting it separately? Mr. Barber advised they were trying to get this 
all done at one time and the applicant is not willing to separate the application. Mrs. 
Lewis asked if there had been an employment study done in the other industrial areas. 
She said when she worked for the Chamber of Commerce, they were always having a 
difficult time finding employees for the warehouses and keeping them staffed. Mr. 
Barber said studies have been done showing that advanced industrial jobs are a missing
component in this county. 

REBUTTAL
Mr. Barber said the character was established as a former mining site. This will provide 
a flourishing economy and has to have employment opportunities. Regarding flooding, 
the City has a flood ordinance that will have to be observed. Regarding the buffer, the 
150 foot buffer will not disturb the tree line, but will preserve it. The walking trail does 
connect by a pedestrian bridge over Camp Creek to connect to Craft Rd. No hazardous 
material uses are proposed in the uses listed as permitted on the site. The urgency 
results from closing a different site and that resulted in a vast increase in volume at this 
existing one. Utilizing bio-mulching and recycling has been done by the county, but not 
everything is able to be recycled. MDEQ sets very specific requirements regarding 
stormwater. There is no targeted site anywhere in the county for this particular use.

STAFF COMMENTS
Mr. Asongayi advised he wanted to answer a few questions raised by the public. With 
regard to the possibility of anyone asking that a Data Center be allowed at this property 
in the future, the law allows anyone to make application to the City. It is incumbent on 
that future board to make the decision to allow that or not. They would have to make an 
application to the City to amend the project text and have to meet the same public notice
requirements advertising the meeting just as we’ve done now. The requirements to 
amend an existing project text are more stringent that building a project text from 
scratch. With regard to improvements being the responsibility of the developer, that is 
standard. Every subdivision is handled that way. Future applications may have an 
exception if they obtain grants, but that infrastructure is handled during the platting
process.

PLANNING COMMISSION FURTHER DISCUSSION
Mr. Jones asked to clarify that the cost of the infrastructure would be to the developer, 
but that it is still the city’s inspectors making sure that it’s done correctly. Mr. Asongayi 
advised that was correct. He said the infrastructure plans would have to be reviewed by 
staff to make sure they meet all city ordinances and regulations before they can begin 

construction. Mr. Dorr said the first motion would be to approve or deny the rezoning and
the second motion would be concerning the project text, if the zoning was approved. Mr.
Asongayi confirmed that was correct. Mrs. Lewis said she feels the city and this board 
are being held hostage by the developer with eminent closure of the current landfill 
because they’ve tied it to a full package to approve with a zoning action, rather than 
having them separated. It makes it difficult with the

Page 1 of 6
 MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT
REGULAR MEETING MAY 14, 2026
The Olive Branch Board of Adjustment meeting was held on Thursday, May 14, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Williams, Vice-Chairman of Board of Zoning Adjustment,
at 6:00 p.m. 
ROLL CALL
Darrel Berkley, William Gray, Aretha Wiseman, Jackie Butler, McKeever Heun, and Carl Williams
were present, and a quorum was established. Ted Roman was absent.
Venard Asongayi,
Director, Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, and Heather
James, Planning Technician, were present from the Planning and Development Department.
THE APPEAL PROCESS
Mr. Williams announced the Appeal Process.
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE APRIL 9, 2026 MEETING
Mr. Williams asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the
April 9, 2026 meeting. Jackie Butler made a motion to approve the minutes. William Gray made
the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Yes Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Absent Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Yes Carl Williams – Yes
OLD BUSINESS
1.
Application for a Conditional Use Permit, submitted by Greg Russell, Civil Source, on
behalf of property owner Kristopher McCord.
The 6.36+/-acre subject property is zoned
M-1, Light Industrial District, and is located north of the intersection of Hwy 178 and
Blocker Street, and immediately north of the BNSF railroad right of way, known as 9490
Hwy 178. The request is to allow for outdoor storage and auctions at this location for a
period of 20 years. (File # CU-26-0003). (Tabled at meeting of April 9, 2026).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Greg Russell, Civil Source, on behalf of property owner Kristopher McCord (Magnolia Auction
Group), requests approval of a conditional use permit for an auction house and outdoor storage of
industrial and construction-related equipment. The Conditional Use Permit request is upon Lot 1,
Magnolia Auction Group Subdivision, for which a final plat was unanimously approved by the Board
of Aldermen at its April 21, 2026 meeting. This lot is located across the BNSF railroad right-of-way
from the northeast corner of Hwy 178 and Blocker St., at 9490 Hwy 178. The entire site is 277,118
sf (±6.36 ac) and is zoned M-1, Light Industrial zoning district. 
The BZA unanimously voted to table this application at the April 9, 2026 to provide time for the
applicant to address pertinent development and operational matters. 

Page 2 of 6
The revised site plan proposes to retain most of the existing on-site buildings. These buildings will
be repainted in a two-tone gray color and an existing temporary office trailer will be removed. The
revised site plan elimiinates references to some existing underground pits and grain conveyance
structures. The City Engineer recommends that these pits be filled prior to the site being used for
business.
An existing chain-link fence encircles ±1.6 ac of the site containing the buildings along the Hwy 178
frontage. The remaining ±4.76 ac is not fenced. The portion of the fence to the west and along the
Hwy 178 frontage is proposed to be removed and replaced with a 6 ft wood fence and landscaping.
Additionally, the applicant proposes to provide a 20 ft wide landscape buffer along the northern
property line.
He also advised that the applicant had performed a decibel test and reported that all activities were
within the allowed levels of the noise ordinance, with the average decibels being 47 at various points
on the property. They performed a mock auction and the reporting decibels were 60 at the rear of
the property and subsequently caught the train at 103 decibels. 

STAFF PRESENTATION
Senior Planner, Kevin Norman, presented the staff report, which is included herein
by reference (File # CU-26-0003).

BOARD OF ZONING ADUSTMENT INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None

PUBLIC HEARING
o
Proponents:

GregRussell,CivilSource,2696DogwoodCircle,Southaven,MS–hehadnothing
to add to the report.

Jeff Waters, 7540 Kelley Cove, Olive Branch, MS – came during discussion on
fence. 
o
Opponents:

None

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
Mr. Williams said this sounds like a really good compromise that covered everything from
last meeting. Mr. Russell said they had worked hard with staff to create something that satisfied all
concerns. Mr. Asongayi wanted to bring up two things. 1. Based on previous discussion, you could
add a condition stating “The noise level of any public address system shall not exceed 60 decibels
at the property line. This also aligns with the noise study that the applicant had done. He said, 60
decibels is the sound of a dishwasher. 75 decibels is the sound of a vacuum cleaner. 2. It has been
standard practice to require composite materials for buffer fence rather than wood. There is a
material similar in cost to wood, but is, in fact, composite and they can use a cap on the fence to
further protect it and to keep out rainwater. Warrior Auto used this material when the Board required
them to use composite. But they failed to put the cap on it. He would recommend including a cap
to protect the fence. The auto shop on Caroma had a chain link fence and had also requested
wood, but this Board required composite instead. Staff has recommended wood because that is
what the applicant has asked for. However, he wanted to call attention to the standard practice that
the Board uses when approving fences for these permits. 

Page 3 of 6
Mr. Waters asked to clarify; are we requiring him to use a composite cap or construct the whole
fence out of composite. Mr. Asongayi said, they have asked for a wood fence. He’s just advising
the Board members of their standard practice to require composite materials rather than wood. Mr.
Waters said that he researched composite materials for fences and the cheapest composite fence
cost $457 per 6 foot section and wood cost $175 per 6 foot section. He’s fine with putting a cap on
a wood fence, but at over 600 feet of fence, the additional costs for composite materials is just too
much cost. He’s fine with a wood or cedar cap, because they do that in residential building, even a
pine fence with a cedar cap, but the composite material costing almost $300 more per each 6 foot
section, that’s far more than what they had budgeted for.
Mrs. Butler asked if they were planning on using pine or cedar. Mr. Waters said they were planning
on a pine fence, but they can use either pine or cedar cap, if they need to. Mrs. Butler said the cap
was for the composite not the wood. Mr. Waters said the wood can warp with rain and weathering,
but the cedar cap would keep out a lot of that rain, even in a wooden fence. Mr. Asongayi said the
composite material he’s referring to is normally used for decking. It looks like wood, but it is
composite. It’s used for decking because it’s flat; water doesn’t seep into the ends. If you turn it on
it’s side and use vertically, you would need to cap that end. He said it’s also been used in dumpster
enclosures. There was a discussion about cost difference and using composite material based on
the original numbers result in an increase in about $30,000.
Mrs. Butler asked about the plants at the border and if they would be watered. Mr. Waters said they
wouldnotbewatered,therewouldjustbeevergreensaddedtotheexistingtreesandthatwillremain
a wooded area. Ms. Wiseman said she prefers 60 decibels at the property line. Mr. Waters said the
decibels of the train coming through is 103 decibels and that happens several times a day. When
they blow the whistle, it increases to 125 decibels. Mr. Williams said he likes the cap idea and that
cedar lasts a long time. Mrs. Butler said this board has required other applicants construct a
composite fence and to allow this one to be made of wood would be setting a precedent for anyone
in the future. Ms. Wiseman agreed that setting a precedent is not something this Board should do.
Mr. Asongayi advised that, after consulting the City Ordinance, the Design Review Ordinance states
that within Commercial and Industrial areas, a wooden fence is strictly prohibited.
Mr. Williams stated, based on this discussion, it sounds like conditions need to be amended as
follows: 
Condition # 4 change to Composite fence
New Condition # 12 Decibels to not exceed 60 decibels at property line from the public address
system.

MOTION

requirements have been met, to approve a Conditional Use Permit for an auction house
and outdoor storage of industrial and construction-related equipment on Lot 1,
Magnolia Auction Group Subdivision, known as 9490 Hwy 178, for a period of 20 years
renewable, subject to the following conditions:
1.
There shall be a mandatory periodic review of the conditional use permit on
May 14, 2027, with continuance of the conditional use permit subject to reviews
every 5 years. Non-compliance with all approval conditions shall be grounds
for revocation of the Conditional use Permit.
2.
Auctions shall be permitted once per week between the hours of 9 am and 9
pm. 

Page 4 of 6
3.
All equipment and materials left from prior industrial operations shall be
removed from the site before the one-year review.
4.
The applicant shall replace the chain link fence along the railway and the
western side of the property with a 6 ft high composite fence with landscaping
as per the submitted site plan. 
5.
A 20 ft landscape buffer shall be maintained between the subject property and
adjacent residential lots to the north. Perimeter buffer planting shall be fully
installed before first auction activity on the property. 
6.
The driveway easement to the property, at its intersection with the railway, shall
be improved to the satisfaction of the City Engineer before commencement of
auction activity on the site.
7.
All existing underground grain pits and structures shall be filled before the site
may be used for auction sales. 
8.
A functional fire hydrant, with pressure that meets the requirements of the fire
code, or as may be approved by the Fire Marshal, must be constructed on site
before any auction activities begin.
9.
All surfaces on which any vehicle will be parked, stored, or driven on shall be
paved within 12 months of approval of this permit.
10. A full set of civil plans shall be provided to City Staff for administrative approval.
11. Any future expansion of the development would require approval by the Board
of Adjustment.
12. Sound level shall not exceed 60 decibels at the property line from the public
address system.
Mr. Gray made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Yes Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Absent Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Yes Carl Williams – Yes
NEW BUSINESS
1.
Application for a Conditional Use Permit, submitted by Roderick Kimmons, on behalf of
property owner Glen Ogden, Ogden Living Trust.
The 0.35 +/- acre property is zoned
C-5 District (Old Towne District) and is located on the north side of Goodman Road E, just
east of the intersection of Pigeon Roost Road and Goodman Road E, known as 9176
Goodman Road E. The request is to allow for an auto shop at this location for a period of
10 years. (File # CU-26- 0004). 

APPLICATION SUMMARY
This request is for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) submitted by Roderick Kimmons on behalf of the
property owner, Glen Ogden (Ogden Living Trust), to allow the operation of an auto repair shop on
approximately 0.35 acres located on the north side of Goodman Road East, just east of the
intersection with Pigeon Roost Road in Olive Branch, Mississippi. The property is zoned C-5 (Old
Towne District), an area intended to promote a pedestrian-oriented, historically compatible mixed-
use environment.
The applicant seeks approval to continue auto repair operations at this location for a period of ten
(10) years. This request follows prior action by the Board of Adjustment regarding Conditional Use
Permit No. CU-21-0005. On February 13, 2025, the Board conducted a follow-up review of the
existing CUP and determined that the operation had not consistently met the required criteria for

Page 5 of 6
conditional uses within the Old Towne District. Specifically, the Board identified concerns related to
compatibility with the district’s character, on-site vehicular congestion, and potential risks to public
health and safety—including documented instances of improper motor oil discharge from within the
building to the rear of the property.
As a result of these findings, the Board amended the original 20-year approval period, reducing it to
a fixed term expiring January 31, 2026, to allow for reassessment and ensure compliance with all
applicable conditions.
In considering this new request for a 10-year CUP, key factors include the applicant’s ability to
demonstrate corrective measures addressing prior violations, adherence to the design and
operational standards of the C-5 Old Towne District, and implementation of site management
practices that mitigate traffic, environmental, and aesthetic impacts. Approval of the request would
require clear and enforceable conditions to ensure the use aligns with the intent of the district and
does not adversely affect surrounding properties or the general welfare of the public.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Associate Planner, Jeremiah McCroskey, presented the staff report, which is
included herein by reference (File # CU-26-0004).

None

o
Proponents:

Roderick Kimmons, 2544 Johnny Walker Rd, Potts Camp, MS – he said the truck
bed is outside to be picked up. He’s trying to keep up the clearance of vehicles at
the end of the day. He’s also working on a new location, and really just needs a
year before he’s ready to move. 
o
Opponents:

None

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
Mrs. Butler said that he’s told he’s told us before he’s working on keeping the site picked up and
there are still the same parking issues. She knows he’s worked hard on this. She asked when he
was going to move the vehicles that are not in spaces? And when the truck in the back with the two
other cars will be towed away. How long will it take you to get to the new place? Mr. Kimmons said
it would be the beginning of 2027. Mr. Heun asked if he will have a lease for the new place? Mr.
Kimmons said he’s working that out with the owner now. He said it’s going to be on Hwy 302 in
Marshall County. Mr. Gray said that he’s got a good business there, but it’s too small for the amount
of work he has taken in. It’s become an eyesore for people driving by. He also said he’s glad he’s
got a bigger place to suit the volume of work he’s got. Ms. Wiseman asked to confirm he’s going to
be out by the first of the year and Mr. Kimmons said yes. Ms. Wiseman said you’re asking us to give
you time to leave and he also said yes. Mr. Gray said his plans for relocation are a good move.
Mr. Gray made a motion to deny and have him vacate the property by Dec 31, 2026.
Mrs. Butler made the second. Before any vote could be taken, Mr. Asongayi advised that they can’t

records.text:
MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH PLANNING COMMISSION
REGULAR MEETING MAY 12, 2026
The Olive Branch Planning Commission meeting was held on Tuesday, May 12, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Dorr, Chairman of Planning Commission, at 6:00 p.m.
ROLL CALL
Janice Lewis, Dion Jones, Diane Senger, Pat Dorr, Steve Stratton and Mark Long were present,
and a quorum was established. Donny Singh was absent. Venard Asongayi, Director, Kevin 
Norman, Senior Planner, Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, and Heather James, 
Planning Technician, were present from the Planning and Development Department. 
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE APRIL 14, 2026 MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the April
14, 2026 meeting. Mr. Stratton made a motion to approve the minutes as presented. Mr. Long
made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Absent Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
CONSENT AGENDA
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
Mr. Dorr announced New Business #1 and noted that there was a request to table until June
9, 2026.
1.
Consideration of an application for the Final Plat Center Hill Farms, Phase 2, submitted by
Alex Gagne, M&R Builders, on behalf of property owner, Johnny McBride. The request is to
create 62 single-family residential lots and 6 common open spaces from 23.78+/-acres. The
subject property is zoned PUD, Planned Unit Development District, and is located on the
west side of Center Hill Rd, beginning at the north end of Lucy Drive. (File #SD-26-0006).
(Applicant requests item to be tabled to June 9, 2026).

MOTION
Ms. Senger made a motion to table the item until June 9, 2026. Mrs. Lewis made 
the second and the motion to table the item was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Absent Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
2.
Consideration of an application for the Preliminary Plat of The Villages at Southbranch,
Phase 4A, submitted by William Kessell, W.H. Porter, on behalf of property owner, Michaelle
Terhune, Southbranch Development LLC.
The request is to create 49 single-family
residential lots and 1 common open space from 14.24+/-acres. The subject property is zoned

R-3, Planned Residential District, and is located at the east end of Sipsey Way, and east of
Bankhead Dr. (File #SD-26-0007). 

APPLICATION SUMMARY
William Kissell, on behalf of the property owner, Southbranch Development, LLC, requests
approval of the preliminary plat for Phase 4A of The Villages at Southbranch Subdivision,
which will consist of 49 single-family residential lots and one 20 ft alley which would provide
access for Lots 210-224. Adjoining streets and utility services are proposed to be extended.
The project text and associated master development plan for this R-3 zoned property was
approved by the Board of Aldermen on January 18, 2022. The preliminary plat aligns with
the provisions of the said project text and associated master layout plan. Staff recommends
approval subject to various conditions.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, presented the staff report, which is included herein
by reference (File # SD-26-0007).

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
Mr. Jones asked to clarify something in section 2.2. He said the report listed 36 cottage 
lots and asked if that was correct. Mr. Norman advised that was a misprint and it should 
be 34 cottage lots.

PUBLIC MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone was present to speak for the application but advised that no
public hearing was required for a plat application.
o
Proponents:

William Kissell, W.H.Porter, 6055 Primacy Pkwy Ste 115, Memphis, TN – 
he had nothing to add.
o
Opponents:

None

PLANNING COMMISISON DISCUSSION
None

MOTION
Mr. Jones made a motion to approve the Preliminary Plat for The Villages at 
Southbranch Subdivision, Phase 4A and recommend same to the Mayor and 
Board of Aldermen subject to the following: 
1.
All improvements shall be the responsibility of the developer and not the 
responsibility of the City of Olive Branch.
2.
All utilities and services (electric, telephone, cable, etc.) shall be installed 
underground. The water service lines shall be installed with tracing wire at
the top.
3.
At final plat consideration, the developer shall submit to the City of Olive 
Branch a letter of credit of sufficient amount as will be determined by the 
City Engineer, plus a 25% contingency, for the completion of all 
uncompleted public improvements required in the land area constitutive of
the Preliminary Plat and for any outstanding As-Built drawings. 

4.
The developer shall submit civil construction plans for grading, 
stormwater management, utilities, streetlights, road construction, and all 
other subdivision infrastructure to the City Engineer and the Director of 
Planning and Development or designee for approval. 
5.
All provisions of the project text and associated preliminary development 
plan for The Villages at Southbranch, as applicable to this phase of the 
subdivision are maintained.
6. “V” shape alley construction is prohibited.
Mr. Long made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Absent Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
3.
Consideration to Amend the Bylaws and Rules of Procedure of the Planning Commission.

SUMMARY
 The amendments proposed herein:

Repeal the conduct of the Planning Commission’s business in accordance with Robert’s
Rules of Order and provides that the Commission shall conduct its business in
accordance with rules adopted by the Planning Commission and by City Ordinance.

Eliminate the administration of oaths and the compelling of witness attendance. The
Planning Commission is neither a final decision making legislative nor judicial or quasi-
judicial body. Its functions generally involve serious consideration of matters before it
and recommendation to the Board of Aldermen.

Codify the order of public hearing that had been considered by the Planning Commission
in the past but not expressly outlined in the Bylaws and Rules of Procedure.

Subordinate the Bylaws and Rules of Procedure to local ordinances and State law.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Venard Asongayi, Director, presented the staff report, which is included herein by
reference.

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None

MOTION
Mrs. Lewis made a motion to approve the item allowing that the language to be repealed is
struck through; the provisions to be adopted are underlined in a full copy of the Bylaws
and Rules of Procedure attached herewith. 
Mr. Stratton made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Absent Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes

OTHER BUSINESS
1.
Discuss draft amendments to the Zoning Ordinance regarding various definitions; restricting
indoor and outdoor smoking in public place establishments within 500 feet of public parks;
specifying criteria for Data Centers as conditional uses in the M-1, Light Industrial, and M-2,
Heavy Industrial Districts only; and limiting the height of free standing monument signs in
the Office (O), Neighborhood Commercial (C-1), (Highway Commercial (C-2), General
Commercial (C-3), and Planned Commercial (C-4) Districts.
Staff provided 25 pages of potential changes for review by the Planning Commission. Changes
were divided into 4 main areas: 
1.
Adding new definitions
2.
Article 4, adding Section 7 (prohibits smoking within 500 feet of city parks
3.
Specifies criteria for Data Centers
4.
Reduces the max height for freestanding signs in certain districts.

Mr. Long asked if this would include chewing tobacco use? Mr. Asongayi said no.

Mr. Jones asked regarding Section 7, can we establish commercial establishments only.
We don’t want to approve something that inhibits companies that allow their employees to
smoke in their breakrooms. Mr. Asongayi said we can add a sentence that this regulation
does not affect designated smoking areas.

Mrs. Lewis asked if the smoking ban refers to the facilities only, or would it include anyone
walking by the park and smoking.
Mr. Asongayi says the smoking ordinance prohibits
anyone smoking in the park.

Mr. Jones asked what if someone wanted to gift the city land next to a cigar bar for a park.
Would that be an issue? Mr. Asongayi said that it would not. If the cigar bar is there first, they
would be allowed to remain, regardless of what comes in afterwards.

Mr. Asongayi explained that Data Centers will require a Conditional Use Permit subject to a
number of conditions. This is about controlling any negative impact to the surrounding areas.
We have to ensure water use does not impact residential areas. We will require the applicant
to do the water study to show how they can use that amount of water and not negatively
impact surrounding areas. These regulations will put pressure on the applicant to provide
that proof. The gas levels will be handled the same way. They have to provide a study
showing noise levels are below a certain threshold at the property line. It needs to be 60
decibels or less. 

Mr. Jones said in the ordinance, we specify solar arrays can be used, but you need a lot of
land to provide that. 40 acres are required to produce 1 megawatt and he’s suggesting that
we take that out as an option. Mr. Asongayi said they can remove solar array.

Water and wastewater reports need to add current and future use to account for the city’s
own growth plans. 

Mrs. Lewis asked what about the data centers and allowing for buffering for heat. It stays so
hot in the summer here anyway, but we don’t want the heat produced by the data centers to
raise the temperature so high that any neighbors to increase their utility bills for additional
cooling. She wants to make them do a study.

Mr. Jones said there is already a provision for waste heat and that they cannot raise the
ambient temperature at the property line at a height of 4 feet.

Mr. Asongayi said the original draft included a distance minimum of 1000 feet from any
residential areas. He said the mayor would like to see 2000 feet minimum. Mr. Asongayi
wants to get this board’s thoughts. Mr. Jones said 1000 feet is a long distance, and if they

comply with all the other requirements and standards discussed (noise, water, waste water,
waste heat) it should be fine at 1000 feet. Mr. Dorr said there will be a room full of people if
they apply for one. Mr. Asongayi said that’s why were are trying to get the right regulations
in place first.

Regarding freestanding signs, Mr. Asongayi said this will just codify what we already have in
place.
On another piece of business, Pat Dorr will be retiring and the June meeting will be his last. At that
meeting, we will elect new officers to begin serving in July.
ADJOURNMENT
Mr. Jones made a motion to adjourn the meeting at 7:11 pm.
Ms. Senger made the second
and the motion was approved as follows: 
Pat Dorr Yes Steve Stratton Yes Donny Singh Absent Dion Jones Yes
Janice Lewis Yes Mark Long Yes Diane Senger Yes

APPROVAL OF MINUTES:

records.text:
MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH PLANNING COMMISSION
REGULAR MEETING APRIL 14, 2026
The Olive Branch Planning Commission meeting was held on Tuesday, April 14, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Dorr, Chairman of Planning Commission, at 6:00 p.m.
ROLL CALL
Janice Lewis, Dion Jones, Diane Senger, Pat Dorr, Donny Singh, Steve Stratton and Mark Long
were present, and a quorum was established. Venard Asongayi, Director, Kevin Norman, Senior
Planner, Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, and Heather James, Planning Technician, 
were present from the Planning and Development Department. 
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE MARCH 10, 2026 MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the March
10, 2026 meeting. Mr. Jones made a motion to approve the minutes as presented. Mr. Long
made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Yes Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
CONSENT AGENDA
OLD BUSINESS
1.
Consideration of an application to amend the Project Text for Trinity Park Planned
Development, submitted by Almotasem Nasser, on behalf of Moheeb Nasser, property
owner.The 16.21+/-acre subject property is zoned PUD, Planned Unit Development, and is
located at the southwest corner of Hwy 305 and Church Rd E, known as 8961 Church Rd.
The request is to add Medical Cannabis as a permitted use within Area 7 of the PUD. (File
# PD-26-0001). (Tabled to this date at meeting of March 10, 2026). 

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Almotasem Nasser, on behalf of property owner, Moheeb Nasser requests to amend
the current project text of the Trinity Park Planned Commercial Development to add “medical
cannabis dispensary” to the list of permitted uses allowed on Lot 1 only of Trinity Park
Subdivision Area 7. The request would not change any existing conditions regarding building
height, location, etc. The modification has been requested by the applicant and should not
disrupt the existing baseline regulations for the current property. Generally, the impact on
neighborhood is not foreseen to be any more than in other commercial districts where
cannabis dispensaries are permitted in the City. Staff recommends approval.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, presented the staff report, which is included
herein by reference (File # PD-26-0001).

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None


PUBLIC HEARING
Mr. Dorr opened the public hearing and asked if anyone was present to speak for the
application.
o
Proponents:

Lauren Ward, Daniel Coker Law Firm, 265 N Lamar Blvd, Ste R, Oxford, 
MS – She stated the Trinity Park Project Text was first approved in 2005 
and Medical Cannabis was not legal at the time. The City Ordinance 
approved medical cannabis in M-1, C1 & C2 Zoning districts. The uses 
currently allowed in the Project Text are Neighborhood Commercial type 
uses, which aligns with the uses in the zoning districts where Medical 
Cannabis is permitted. This particular use is heavily regulated at the 
state and local level. There are Cannabis applications that are still 
required to be submitted and approved at both the state and local levels 
before he can move forward with his business. Approval of this 
application just gives the applicant permission to move forward with those
cannabis applications. This is also heavily regulated by Mississippi Dept 
of Health – this is similar to any other pharmacy. A prescription is written 
by a doctor and taken here to be filled. It cannot be consumed at this 
location. It is for Medical Use only. 
o
Opponents:

Dean Stewart, 4596 N Terrace Stone Dr, Olive Branch, MS – He is the 
Pastor at Labelle Haven Baptist Church. He wants to know what the 
City’s plans for the Church Rd & Hwy 305 area are moving forward. 
Allowing this use will limit what moves into the area in the future. The 
church has spent millions on upgrades to the church and have plans for a
new facility to serve as a respite center. The city has also spent millions 
on the state of the art soccer complex directly across the street from this 
location. This proposed use is being considered between 2 entrances of 
Bell Ridge Subdivision. Permitting this will devalue the neighborhood. 
This use is not compatible with this area, a soccer complex, church and 
neighborhood. Says there is a closer location on his property that would 
have prevented this without allowance of a waiver. 

Jarquiste Rogers, 8649 S Trinity Park Dr, Olive Branch, MS – He agrees 
with the Pastor. The City just spent $4.7 million on the soccer complexes.
This is not a pharmacy. This is selling a specific product. Wants to know 
why they want to do this location and why not somewhere else. The city 
needs to grow in a manner that is strategic and this use does not support 
that. He sits on the HOA board of his neighborhood. He says his house 
will back up to this location and this is not what we want here. He 
believes that growth must be strategic, not quick. He worries that this will 
attract crime. It’s too close to his house. The original plan was to be a 
multi-use hotel property. He said he came to oppose the addition of the 
convenience store also. He doesn’t want the property values to drop. He
said the safety of kids is affected. He doesn’t want “riffraff” from Memphis
coming here to purchase these products. He wants them to stay away.

REBUTTAL

Lauren Ward spoke to some of the concerns raised by the citizens. Regarding it being 
too close to the church, the state has set the statute regarding Medical Cannabis and the
distance, and how to measure that distance. This property is in compliance. The statute
also states the protected uses that a buffer is appropriate for. To consider the soccer 
fields is not within the laws that exist. There is no documentation that the CVS has 
poorly affected the soccer complex. The proposed use is similar; coming to pick up a 
prescribed medication and leaving. There is no proof that this will devalue anything, but 
this was always intended to allow commercial uses. The use fits within the 
Comprehensive Plan and the Zoning Ordinance that already allow this use in other 
zoning districts. This is a heavily regulated use on a state and federal level, including 
any security plans for this location. 
Almotasem Nasser, 3930 Pleasant Hill Rd, Olive Branch, MS also offered rebuttal to the 
concerns. Mr. Nasser said there is a very specific security plan that has to follow state 
and federal laws. There is a well defined metric system that tracks the product from 
beginning to end. The regulations are stringent in product, training, employees, storage, 
etc. There should be no “riffraff” from Memphis. They would not be allowed to purchase
anything because they can only sell to someone living in Mississippi prescribed by a 
Mississippi doctor. He said that THC8 is allowed in Mississippi. Anyone from Memphis 
can go to any gas station between the state line and this location to buy that and never 
have to venture to this area. The security is heightened already due to these state 
regulations, making any issues unlikely. If the worst happens, they would take a step 
back and have an even heavier security plan. 

PLANNING COMMISISON DISCUSSION
Mr. Jones asked staff if there was any truth to the statement that there was a closer 
building entrance from which the buffer zone to the nearest property of the La Belle 
Baptist Church could be measured, which would result in the site note meeting the 
1,000ft separation requirement. Dr. Asongayi said the state Statute reads that the 
1,000ft distance is measured from the main point of entry of the Cannabis facility to the 
nearest property line of the protected entity (church, daycare or school). The distance 
from the front door of this suite number to the closest property line of the church is 
1001.47 feet per the surveyor’s submission. Mr. Jones asked to clarify that the state 
made the requirement and did not give room for the local municipality to change that. 
Dr. Asongayi confirmed that the 1,000ft requirement is State law. Mr. Jones asked if 
Medical Cannabis was a permitted use in C-1 and Dr. Asongayi confirmed that it was.
Mr. Jones said this Commission has to look at precedents and state laws as they are 
written, not our personal opinion. Zoning is a legal issue and we have to make 
recommendations based on the laws that exist. He asked when the Board of Aldermen 
would hear this item. Dr. Asongayi advised the public hearing in front of the Board of 
Aldermen would be on May 19th. Dr. Asongayi said that public parks are not listed as 
one of the sensitive/protected uses in State law, although a reasonable compatibility 
argument can be made. While recreational use may have a more overt effect on public 
park users, medical use impact on pubic parks may be insignificant. 
Mr. Singh said it’s very difficult to say that this doesn’t fit within the area. C1 and C2 
Districts already allow it. This Planned Development was intended to hold similar uses. 
The law is the law and we have to abide by that. If this were being brought into a C1 or 

a C2 district, this board wouldn’t even get the opportunity to hear this; it’s permitted 
outright, within those distance restrictions. Mrs. Lewis said the Board of Aldermen 
considers this after we do. We do have to follow the law and you’ll have the opportunity 
to speak at the Board of Aldermen meeting. She asked Mr. Nasser why this location 
was selected over some other location and asked if there was consideration other than 
it’s already owned by your family. He advised that they do ow it, and there is not another
dispensary close to this location. The next closest is a bit of a drive and this is a 
convenient location. He said that if someone is injured and they go to a hospital, they 
are prescribed opioids and they can be picked up at any pharmacy. This is less 
dangerous and more heavily regulated than opioids. Mr. Long said he is concerned that 
children visit the park which is right across the street.

MOTION
Mr. Jones made a motion to approve the application as presented, subject to
conditions as outlined in the staff’s written report, and Mrs. Lewis made the
second. There was an initial call for a vote producing an apparent 3-3 result, with Mr.
Singh initially attempting to abstain. After discussion, the Chairman called for
clarification of how members were voting on the motion, which indicated that the
result was a 4-3 positive vote (with no abstention) to recommend the item to the Board
of Aldermen for approval as specified below. This recommendation was based on the
following findings:
1.
The proposed amendment is consistent with the intent and purpose of the
Trinity Park PUD, specifically Area 7. The Comprehensive Plan designates
this area as “Neighborhood Commercial,” and the inclusion of “Medical
Cannabis
Dispensary”
as
a
permitted
use
is
compatible
with
that
designation. 
2.
Given the arterial classification of Highway 305, the addition of a “medical
cannabis dispensary” as a use-by-right is not expected to result in
inadequate street capacity, nor will it adversely affect traffic volumes along
Highway 305 or Church Road or create unsafe access conditions to the
subject property. 
3.
The proposed use will not overburden public utilities, drainage systems, or
community facilities, nor will it increase the risk of fire, flood, or otherwise
endanger public health, safety, or welfare. 
4.
The location of the Medical Cannabis Dispensary would meet the minimum
