School, Daycare facilities.
Pat Dorr - Yes
Steve Stratton - No
Donny Singh - Yes
Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - No Diane Senger - No
2.
Consideration of an application for a Zoning Map Amendment, submitted by Michel Lebel,
Allen & Hoshall, on behalf of property owner Desoto County School District. The request is
to rezone 42.5+/-acres from PUD, Planned Unit Development and M-1, Light Industrial
District, to A-R, Agricultural-Residential District. The subject property is located on the east
side of Craft Rd, in the southeast corner of the future expansion of W Sandidge Rd and Craft
Rd. (File # RZN-26-0001). (Tabled to this date at meeting of March 10, 2026).

APPLICATION SUMMARY

The applicant, Michel Lebel, Allen & Hoshall, on behalf of Desoto County School
District, the property owner, requests (1) extrication of ±35.99 acres from the Funderburk
Planned Unit Development (PUD) and the rezoning of this area from PUD to Agricultural
Residential (A-R), and the rezoning of a 6.51ac westerly adjoining parcel from M-1, Light
Industrial District, to A-R. The property owner currently intends to construct a Desoto County
School District Career Tech. Center on the site. A school is neither a permitted nor a
conditional use in either the concerned area of the said PUD or the M-1 District; hence, the
rezoning is necessary. Public schools are permitted by right in the A-R District. The applicant
avows that the current PUD zoning did not anticipate the long-term need for educational
infrastructure and work force development in the City that could be provided at the concerned
location. While the land area to the east of the site has developed as light industrial in the
last two decades, adjoining parcels to the north and the land area west of Craft Rd in the
vicinity of the subject property have remained undeveloped agricultural land. The Future
Land Use Map in the City’s Comprehensive Plan 2040, which articulates the land use public
need policies of the City, designates most of the site as “Public / Semi-Public” and a small
southern portion as “Technology / Employment Center.” The requested rezoning aligns with
these land use character of the area and public need. Therefore, staff recommends approval.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Venard Asongayi, Director, presented the staff report, which is included herein by
reference (File # RZN-26-0001).

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
Mr. Jones asked if there is a step that the Planning Commission could take that 
would not leave the property as AR? Mr. Asongayi said you could recommend a different
district. The reason that AR was selected is that the updated Zoning Ordinance will 
include a new district, Institutional District. This property will convert over to that upon 
approval and adoption of the Ordinance. In the meantime, this would either be AR or 
R3, which is another planned development and across the street is already there. 

PUBLIC HEARING
Mr. Dorr opened the public hearing and asked if anyone was present to speak for the
application.
o
Proponents:

Michel Lebel, Architect and Project Manager, 1661 International Dr, 
Memphis, TN – He had nothing to add
o
Opponents:

None

PLANNING COMMISISON DISCUSSION
Mr. Singh asked if there was a proposed timeline. Michel said they are trying to open by
Fall of 2028.

MOTION
Mr. Singh made a motion, based on a finding that the character of the subject
property area has changed in the last twenty years from vacant land to light
industrial
warehouses
with
increasing
technical
workforce
needs
and
undeveloped land has remained agricultural, which the requested rezoning aligns
with, and that there is a public need for the rezoning as evident in the Future Land
Use Map designation of the property, to recommend that the Board of Aldermen:

(1) Extricate a ±35.99 acres area from the Funderburk Planned Unit
Development (PUD), being a portion of the R.R. Bridgeforth Heirs
Partnership, GP per Bk 439-361 (3/7/2003), Parcel 2, and rezoning it from
PUD to A-R, Agricultural Residential.
(2) Rezone a ±6.51ac part of the Whitten Land Co. property as recorded in
Bk 1006-733, Tract 1, from Light Industrial District (M-1) to A-R,
Agricultural Residential District.
Mr. Stratton made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Yes Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
NEW BUSINESS
1.
Consideration of an application for the Final Plat of Magnolia Auction Group, submitted by
Greg Russell, Civil Source, on behalf of property owner, Kristopher McCord. The request is
to create a single industrial lot of 6.36+/-acres. The subject property is zoned M-1, Light
Industrial District, and is located on the northeast corner of Hwy 178 and Blocker Street,
known as 9490 Hwy 178. (File #SD-26-0005).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Greg Russell, Civil Source, on behalf of property owner Kristopher McCord (Magnolia
Auction Group) requests approval of the final plat for Lot 1, Magnolia Auction Group
Subdivision. The proposed lot is located directly across the Hwy 178 and BNSF Railroad
rights-of-way from the northeast corner of the intersection of Hwy 178 and Blocker Street,
known as 9490 Hwy 178. The subdivision plat will consist of one 6.36 ac lot, which is zoned
M-1, Light Industrial. The M-1 zoning district does not have a minimum lot area requirement.
Existing public utilities in the vicinity are primarily located within the Hwy 178 right-of-way,
with one 8-inch gravity sewer line shown running northward from the subject parcel. There
are existing public fire hydrants located within the Hwy 178 right-of-way, with one private
hydrant located near the eastern property line. Access would be by a 50 ft easement crossing
the BNSF right-of-way. Staff recommends approval subject to various conditions. 

STAFF PRESENTATION
Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, presented the staff report, which is included herein
by reference (File # SD-26-0005).

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None

PUBLIC MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone was present to speak for the application but advised that no
public hearing was required for a plat application.
o
Proponents:

had nothing to add.

None

MOTION
Mr. Stratton made a motion to approve the final plat for Magnolia Auction Group
and recommend same to the Board of Aldermen subject to the following: 
1.
The Final Plat shall be recorded before any new construction upon Lot 1.
2.
Improvements
shall
be
the
responsibility
of
the
developer
and
not
the
responsibility of the City of Olive Branch.
3.
It shall be the responsibility of the property owner to ensure that the hydrant along
the east property line meets flow requirements as stipulated by the current
applicable fire codes of the City of Olive Branch before the plat is recorded. It shall
be the responsibility of the Fire Marshal to ascertain and certify that this
requirement is met.
4.
The hydrant shall also be replaced with a current model hydrant as per the
agreement between the applicant and the City of Olive Branch.
Ms. Senger made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Yes Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
OTHER BUSINESS

Zoning Ordinance Updates

were a number of points to go over.

In the
future, when the Zoning Ordinance is adopted, we will see (current) AR district
split into two separate districts, AR (as it looks now) and Rural Estate.
Rural
Estate will require a minimum of 1-2 acres per lot.
It will allow open ditches.
Light will be minimized to a degree. Lighting is a significant element to promote

records.summary: Page 1 of 6 MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT REGULAR MEETING APRIL 9, 2026 The Olive Branch Board of Adjustment meeting was held on Thursday, April 9, 2026, in the Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m. CALL TO ORDER The meeting was called to order by Mr. Roman, Chairman of Board of Zoning Adjustment, at 6:00 p.m. ROLL CALL Ted Roman, W
records.text:
Page 1 of 6
 MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT
REGULAR MEETING APRIL 9, 2026
The Olive Branch Board of Adjustment meeting was held on Thursday, April 9, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Roman, Chairman of Board of Zoning Adjustment, at 
6:00 p.m. 
ROLL CALL
Ted Roman, William Gray, Aretha Wiseman, Jackie Butler, McKeever Heun, and Carl Williams
were present, and a quorum was established. Darrel Berkley was absent.
Venard Asongayi,
Director, Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, and Heather
James, Planning Technician, were present from the Planning and Development Department.
THE APPEAL PROCESS
Mr. Roman announced the Appeal Process.
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE MARCH 12, 2026 MEETING
Mr. Roman asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the
March 12, 2026 meeting. Carl Williams made a motion to approve the minutes. Jackie Butler
made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Yes Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Absent Carl Williams – Yes
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
Mr. McCroskey advised the applicant for New Business #1 had gotten delayed at work, but
that her daughter was enroute to represent the item. He asked the Chairman if he wanted
to table the item. Mr. Roman said we would just reverse order to give them time to appear
and hear Item # 2 first.
2.
Application for a Conditional Use Permit, submitted by Greg Russell, Civil Source, on
behalf of property owner Kristopher McCord.
The 6.36+/-acre subject property is zoned
M-1, Light Industrial District, and is located north of the intersection of Hwy 178 and
Blocker Street, and immediately north of the BNSF railroad right of way, known as 9490
Hwy 178. The request is to allow for outdoor storage and auctions at this location for a
period of 20 years. (File # CU-26-0003).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Greg Russell, Civil Source, on behalf of property owner Kristopher McCord (Magnolia Auction
Group), requests approval of a conditional use permit for an auction house and outdoor storage of
industrialandconstruction-relatedequipment.TheConditionalUsePermitrequestisuponproposed

Page 2 of 6
Lot 1, Magnolia Auction Group Subdivision. This lot is located across the BNSF railroad right-of-way
from the northeast corner of Hwy 178 and Blocker St., at 9490 Hwy 178. The entirety of the site is
277,118 sf (±6.36 ac) and is zoned M-1 Light Industrial zoning district. 
The applicant has submitted a site development plan that retains most of the existing on-site
buildings. These buildings will be repainted in a two-tone gray color. The applicant has stated an
existing temporary office trailer will be removed and several existing underground pits and grain
conveyance structures that will eventually be abandoned and filled.
An existing chain-link fence enclosing ±1.6 ac of the site with the buildings and along the Hwy 178
frontage is proposed to be removed and replaced with a 6 ft wood fence. The remaining 4.76 ac is
unfenced. A landscape plan has not been submitted.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Senior Planner, Kevin Norman, presented the staff report, which is included herein
by reference (File # CU-26-0003).

BOARD OF ZONING ADUSTMENT INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
Mr. Williams asked what parking requirements would this have for visitors, in numbers? Mr. Norman
said he would need to double check the numbers and that it was proposed that the eastern side of
the property would be paved for exhibits and with a separate area for patrons. 

PUBLIC HEARING
o
Proponents:

Jeff Waters, 7540 Kelley Cove, Olive Branch, MS – he advised he is in real estate
primarily, but is a partner in Magnolia Auction Group. They are currently under
contract and within their due diligence period. We would be working within the
fenced area and the east grassy area will be left alone. He said there are 2 parts to
the auction, 1 in person & 1 online. Their auctions are similar to ebay regarding the
online portion. Items may be brought in up to 1 week prior to the auction date and
gone within 2-3 days after the auction is over. These will be primarily on Saturday.
Some auctions may not even have products on site, but pictures instead. It will
take about 6-8 months to get ready. A lot of the fenced area is paved, but you can’t
see it because of all the stuff that is there. They are planning on removing all of that
old stuff and filling in all the pits with gravel. They will clean up the property and
make it look nicer. This is an M-1 property and will be lower impact than most other
M-1 uses. There should only be 1 employee on site. 

Greg Russell, Civil Source, 2696 Dogwood Circle, Southaven, MS – he said there
is a lot of stuff there; so much, it’s hard to see from aerial photos. From a city
standpoint, the amount of cleanup will be beneficial. Even if a tractor is stored there
unexpectedly for 2 weeks, no one will see it. 
o
Opponents:

Bob Rice, 369 Surrey Loop, Byhalia, MS – He’s representing the Morris Walker
family – they own property at 7166 Westbranch Rd and 20 other rental properties
in the area. 9555 Goodman Rd is one of those properties. They would also like a
buffer. Even with the 100 foot tree buffer, they are concerned about visibility and
lighting issues. They want assurance that lighting will not spill over to the residential
area.
He is also concerned about the noise spillover with the PA speakers,
especially not knowing if there are going to be late nights. He is worried about the
financial impact on his property and being able to rent in the future. 

Page 3 of 6

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
Mr. Roman asked if there would be any fuel storage on site. Mr. Waters advised there would
not be. The old fuel tanks on site will be sold, and there are no buried fuel tanks. The only fuel that
would be there would be the vehicles they own. Ms. Wiseman asked what type of equipment they
are looking to auction. Mr. Waters said it would primarily be heavy equipment and farm equipment.
He said some is on consignment to them pending sale. He said they would normally be on site from
Wednesday – Saturday. Mr. Roman asked if something doesn’t sell, if the owner comes back to
retrieve the items. Mr. Waters advised they would come back. Mr. Gray asked if the entire sales
area was paved. Mr. Waters advised yes that everything inside the fence is paved. He said there
are two 40 – foot containers that they will need to empty, inventory and then sell or get rid of. The
east side of the property will be left alone, but they would maintain the grass and keep it cut. They
may expand in the future but would come back to this Board to ask for that approval at a later date.
Mr. Russell wanted to address some of the conditions: (1)1 per month was an estimate, but may
happen more often than that. He wants that condition removed. If a vehicle auction (for example)
presents itself, they don’t want to limit themselves and miss that opportunity. (2) He’s also asking
that the condition requiring all equipment and materials to be removed before the first auction be
removed because it’s just not feasible.
Some of this work will take cranes to be removed.
Additionally, some of that equipment and materials will be part of an auction to be held at the site.
(3) Regarding the landscape requirement, this is M1and backs up to a residential area. There are
mature trees between the two areas. They will dedicate a 40 foot buffer and show any holes filled
in. (5) For the ingress/egress road improvements; this is not a road, it’s a driveway, and once the
railroad track is crossed, it is an access easement on private property. Requiring an engineering
report would potentially create problems for the neighbors. They think there are large trucks tearing
the road up and creating a hump over the tracks. There is no hump there now. (6) They don’t mind
submitting a report on available utilities. (7) The safety pits will be filled in and (8) they will come up
with a parking plan, but a good portion is already paved and there are some additional gravel areas.
Adjacent properties have cars everywhere on the gravel and the grass. They agree with the
conditions 9-12. Everything in the fence is already paved and they will come back to this Board for
approvalofanychanges. They’veaskedfor20yearstomatchthelengthoftheloanfortheproperty.
 The bank may reconsider loaning the money if the term of the approval is less than that. 
Mr. Roman asked if it was a likelihood that auctions would happen during the week. Mr. Russell
said maybe not; the plan is for Saturdays, but anything could happen. Mr. Roman said this road
does get traffic and he’s worried that this will disrupt that traffic. Mr. Russell asked who they would
be disturbing. Ms. Wiseman said the residents and the business owners that work in that area.
Yes, it’s been vacant for 20 years, but this development could disrupt those in the area. Mr. Russell
said there are no other residences except the ones that front Goodman. They are 100 feet from the
woods, but 800 feet away from the business. He asked about the bar across the street and how
that doesn’t disrupt the neighbors. 
Mr. Roman said that he understands more than once a month doesn’t seem like a lot, but to allow it
just anytime isn’t great either. This property will add traffic regardless. Mrs. Butler said there is a
school close, so safety for the kids is a concern. There are also other business owners in that area
thatutilizeHwy178andadditionaltrafficonHwy178. Mr.Russellsaidthatwhentheboringcompany
was there, there was a lot of traffic. Mrs. Butler said she’s been to these types of auctions, and
sometimes there are hundreds of people. Mr. Williams said that some of the businesses along Hwy
178 are open on Saturdays. Mrs. Butler said that there must be a plan with an ADA requirement.
Mr. Heun asked if they would agree that the occupancy level determined the number of parking
spaces? Where would the extra people park? Mr. Russell said there is a gravel lot next door. Mr.
Heun said there’s just not enough information to see a plan. Mr. Waters said there is no definitive

Page 4 of 6
plan, as they can’t predict attendance; he wishes they could, but it’s still a low impact use for M-1
zoned property. There could be a warehouse running 3 shifts there based on zoning alone. Ms.
Wiseman is concerned that there will be a sound issue for the surrounding neighbors. 
Mrs. Butler agrees this will make the property look much better, but we want this to be a good
neighbor to the surrounding area. She is worried about heavy equipment coming up the street and
blockingtraffic. Mr.WilliamsaskedwhattypeofPAsystemtheywereplanningonusing. Mr.Waters
said either a truck with 2 speakers or handheld microphones. He said the sound won’t carry outside
the area that much. Mr. Williams said he is worried about spillover parking to the opposite side of
the street. Potential buyers would be bringing trailers to take equipment they buy home. Mr. Waters
said there is plenty of parking and shouldn’t be any parking across the street. 
Mr. Asongayi said the board has raised a number of concerns, and without plans in your hands, he
doesn’t know if we can answer those concerns tonight. He understands this is under contract, and
asked the applicant if it could be extended to work out these concerns and bring back to the BZA
next month? Yes, we want the property cleaned up, but these other concerns are valid. Mr. Waters
said the bank may or may not extend, he doesn’t have final say. It would have to be in writing and
no idea what that answer may be. 
Ms. Wiseman said her biggest concern is that they were asking for exceptions to some of the more
major conditions. Mr. Heun asked what maintenance agreement is in place? Are you willing to sign
for one of the other 2 businesses? Mr. Waters said that shared area is not in disrepair. The road, in
places, is 3 feet higher than the building entrances. That will create flooding of those buildings. 
Mr. Heun said he doesn’t think this maintaining that entrance should be all on the applicant, but
shared by the others who access it. The maintenance agreement will protect you too. He said it’s
hard to make a decision, without certainty of a parking plan, there’s just not enough information to
make a decision. Mr. Williams suggested that the applicant work with staff on a better number for
on-site auctions. There has to be a limit on it. They can’t allow them to be held every day. He likes
the idea of some being online. Mr. Waters said he wishes he could tell you there wouldn’t be a lot,
but he just doesn’t know. Mr. Williams said there are just too many loose ends and too many
unanswered questions. He thinks this is a great idea for the property, but too many loose ends to
make a definitive decision. 
Mr. Heun asked Mr. Rice if there were any street names in surrounding areas that were estimated
to be impacted by this. Mr. Rice said Goodman Rd would be impacted, both the residential and
commercialproperties. Mrs.Butlersaidtherearejusttoomanyunansweredquestions. Mr.Williams
said he would like to see this happen, but not without closing some of these loopholes. He thinks it’s
a good idea for this property and suggesting adding a condition that all auctions must be held during
daylight hours. He just thinks there’s more work to be done to the plan. Mr. Roman said it started
off good, but now they are looking to be held anytime. Mr. Williams and Mr. Gray agreed that it was
a good idea to table. Staff and the board were provided images of the entrance over the railroad
tracks, across the shared easement and the driveway to the property.

MOTION
Mrs. Butler made the motion to table the item until the May meeting (May 14th) to get questions
answered. Mr. Gray made the second and the motion to table was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Yes Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Absent Carl Williams – Yes

Page 5 of 6
Mr. Russell asked that the Board not table, but rather, make a ruling tonight. Mr. Williams advised
that the item had already been tabled and the public hearing was closed.
1.
Application for a Zoning Variance, submitted by Sherice Jones, property owner.
The
0.22+/-acre subject property is zoned R-3, Planned Residential District, and is located on
the east side of Farguson Cove, approximately 275 feet south of Sanford Dr, known as
Lot 22, College Crossing, at 4128 Farguson Cove. The request is to encroach 3 feet into
the 5-foot side setback for the construction of a 20’ by 20’ accessory building. (File # VR-
26-0002).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Sherice Jones, property owner, is requesting approval of a variance from the side
yard setback requirement of the approved College Crossing Subdivision, R-3 Single-
Family-Residential in order to allow the construction of an accessory building 3 feet into
the side yard setback of Lot 22, more specifically known as 4128 Farguson Cove. Article
VII, Sec.2(B)(3)(b)(iii) of the Zoning Ordinance stipulates that accessory building that are
at least ten (10) feet from the principal residence should be located at least 5ft from the
side property line. The applicant, request a 3ft variance from this side yard setback based
on the irregular shape and comparatively small size of the lot.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Associate Planner, Jeremiah McCroskey, presented the staff report, which is
included herein by reference (File # VR-26-0002).

BOARD OF ZONING ADUSTMENT INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
Mr. Williams asked if construction material was discussed. Mr. McCroskey said this is a
standard metal building kit in a box, but would be behind a 6 foot fence in a cove.

PUBLIC HEARING
o
Proponents:

Rashonda Johnson, 4128 Farguson Cove – she is applicant’s daughter. She had
nothing to add to the report.
o
Opponents:

Darren Curtis, 4146 Farguson Cove, Olive Branch, MS – he said he wasn’t for or
against, he just wanted to know where would it be on her property. Mr. Roman
advised it would be completely behind her fence in the back yard. Mr. Curtis asked
if it would fit, and Mr. Roman advised it would.

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
Mr. Williams asked if it would be a garage type door. Ms. Johnson said she had a picture
and showed the board. Mr. Roman asked if there was any HOA and there is not. Ms. Wiseman
askedifthecurrentstructurewouldberemoved. Mr.McCroskeysaiditwouldnot,thatithadalready
been permitted, but said it may be able to be moved if it needed to be. Mr. Williams said it would be
a tight fit, but it works. 

MOTION
Mr. Gray made a motion, based on finding that a hardship exists, namely a small size
corner lot relative to the sizes of other surrounding lots, and all the criteria have been met,
approve an encroachment of 3 feet into the 5-foot side setback for the construction of a 20’
by 20’ accessory building at 4128 Farguson CV subject to the applicant obtaining a building
permit before construction.

Page 6 of 6
Mrs. Butler made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Yes Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Absent Carl Williams – Yes
OTHER BUSINESS
1.
Update regarding the Conditional Use Permit granted by the Board of (Zoning) Adjustment
on May 13, 2021 (File # CU21-0005) to allow an auto repair shop in the C-5, Old Towne
District. The 0.35 +/- acre property is located on the north side of Goodman Road E, just
east of the intersection of Pigeon Roost Road and Goodman Road E, known as 9176
Goodman Road E. 
Mr. Asongayi advised it was not necessary to have on the agenda and no discussion was
warranted.
ADJOURNMENT
Mrs. Butler made a motion to adjourn the meeting at 7:32pm.
Ms. Wiseman made the
second and the motion was approved as follows: 
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Yes Aretha Wiseman – Yes

MINUTE SUMMARY 1 
APRIL 7, 2026 

BE IT REMEMBERED that the Mayor and Board of Aldermen of the City 
of Olive Branch met in regular session, April 7, 2026 at 6:00 o’clock 
p.m., in the Municipal Court Room at 6900 Highland Street. 
 
AGENDA 
 
Mayor Adams called the regular meeting to order at 6:00 
o’clock p.m. 

Pastor Jerrod Brooks, First Baptist Church had the opening 
prayer. Mayor Adams led the Pledge of Allegiance. 

ROLL CALL (Establish Quorum): 
 
The City Clerk called roll to establish quorum with the 
following members present to wit: Mayor Kenneth R. Adams, 
Alderwoman Jan Aldridge, Alderman George Collins, Alderman Dale 
Dickerson, Alderman Gil Earhart, Alderman Don Gammage and 
Alderwoman Pat Hamilton. These members constitute a quorum. 
Alderman David Wallace was not present. Also present were Tena 
Stewart, City Clerk and Bryan Dye, City Attorney. 

APPROVAL OF MINUTES: 
 
Minutes of the Regular Meeting held March 17, 2026, approved 
as presented, motion carried with Alderwoman Aldridge, Alderman 
Collins, Alderman Dickerson, Alderman Gammage, and Alderwoman 
Hamilton voting in favor, with Alderman Earhart abstaining, and 
with Alderman Wallace being absent. 

PUBLIC COMMENTS: 
 
1. Ms. Jenna Kern, with the DeSoto County Dream Center, addressed 
the Board with updates regarding the Dream Center. Ms. Kern 
announced the organization is expanding into the City of Olive 
Branch with a new facility at 8606 Old HWY 78. 
 
2. Mr. John Wilson, with Light the Way, addressed the Board and 
provided an update about the upcoming July 3rd Independence 
Day festival to be held at the City Park. The festival will 
be free of charge again this year, and headliners will be 
announced soon on Light the Way social media. 
 
3. Ms. Lisa Clark, representing Winshape Camps Olive Branch, 
addressed the Board regarding the organization’s summer camp 
to be held June 29, 2026 through July 3, 2026. Ms. Clark 
asked the City to help promote the camp through its social 
media platforms and City signs.

Customer Service Clerk Terry Green with a privately-funded 
monetary recognition. Terry went outside to assist a drive-thru 
utility customer with their payment and recognized signs of medical

distress. Terry’s actions initiated a call for medical assistance 
for this individual.

High School’s boys’ soccer team for winning the 2026 Class 6A State 
Championship. Team members include Aidan Anewalt, Aiden Masters,

 Mayor Adams and the Board of Aldermen recognized Center Hill

Elijah Westbrook.

records.text:
Page 1 of 5
 MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT
REGULAR MEETING MARCH 12, 2026
The Olive Branch Board of Adjustment meeting was held on Thursday, February 12, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Roman, Chairman of Board of Zoning Adjustment, at 
6:00 p.m. 
ROLL CALL
Ted Roman, William Gray, Aretha Wiseman, Jackie Butler and Carl Williams were present, and
a quorum was established. McKeever Heun and Darrel Berkley were absent. Venard Asongayi,
Director, Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, and Heather
James, Planning Technician, were present from the Planning and Development Department.
THE APPEAL PROCESS
Mr. Roman announced the Appeal Process.
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE FEBRUARY 12, 2026 MEETING
Mr. Roman asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the
December 11, 2025 meeting.
William Gray made a motion to approve the minutes.
Aretha
Wiseman made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Absent Carl Williams – Yes
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
1.
Application for a Conditional Use Permit, submitted by Amanda Lacey, AERC PLLC, on behalf of
property owner SM Lawrence.
The 0.68+/-acre subject property is zoned C-2, Highway
Commercial District, and is located on the northwest side of Industrial Dr approximately
840 feet west of Old Craft Rd, known as Lot 12, Craft Road Industrial Park, 8211 Industrial
DR. The request is to allow for outdoor storage at this location for a period of 20 years. (File # CU-
26-0002).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Amanda Lacey, AERC PLLC, on behalf of SM Lawrence, property owner, 
requests approval of a conditional use permit for outdoor storage of HVAC materials at 
8211 Industrial Dr. upon proposed Lot 12A, Craft Road Industrial Park. The subject 
property is located on the northwest side of Industrial Dr., approximately 840 ft west of 
Old Craft Rd. The applicant has submitted a site development plan that includes a 
±21,580 sf fenced-in concrete and limestone HVAC laydown storage area. The applicant
has proposed a 6ft. high composite screening fence to screen the front of the storage 
area, with a 6 ft. chain-link fence enclosing the rear of the storage area. A landscape 

Page 2 of 5
plan has also been submitted that screens the front and complies with the landscape 
ordinance.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Senior Planner, Kevin Norman, presented the staff report, which is included herein
by reference (File # CU-26-0002).

BOARD OF ZONING ADUSTMENT INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
Mr. Roman wanted to make sure the date in Condition # 6 is corrected to 2026. It was just
a typo.

PUBLIC HEARING
o
Proponents:

Robbie Meredith, AERC, 342 W Valley St, Hernando, MS – He said there will be
limestone in the lot and surrounded by a 6 foot composite fence. There shouldn’t
be anything visible from the road.
o
Opponents:

None

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
Mr. Gray said there are lots of trees already and it will be well screened from Hwy 78.

MOTION
Mr. Williams made a motion, based on the Board of Adjustment’s finding that all
requirements have been met, to approve a Conditional Use Permit for a “contractor’s yard or
storage, outdoor” on proposed Lot 12A of Craft Road Industrial Park Subdivision, known as 8211
Industrial Dr, for a period of 20 years subject to the following conditions:
1.
All materials stored outdoors must be fully screened in length, width, and height from view
from Industrial Dr, using a composite fence.
2.
The use of compacted limestone is only permitted in material storage areas. All drive isles
and parking areas within and outside the storage area must be paved. 
3.
A full set of civil and landscaping plans shall be provided to City Staff for administrative
approval. The landscape plan must provide vegetative screening along the fence as the
Director of Development Services or designee shall find satisfactory.
4.
Any future expansion of the development would require approval by the Board of
Adjustment.
5.
All materials stored outdoors must meet requirements of the Fire Code.
6.
Mandatory periodic review of the conditional use permit every two years from March 12,
2025, with continuance of the conditional use permit subject to compliance with approval
conditions No. 1 to 5 above.
Mrs. Butler made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Absent Carl Williams – Yes
OTHER BUSINESS

Page 3 of 5
1.
Update regarding the Conditional Use Permit granted by the Board of (Zoning) Adjustment
on October 10, 2019 (File # CU19-0013) to allow a towing service in the C-2, Highway
Commercial District. The 2.94+/- acre property is located on the north side of Caroma
Street and west of HWY 305, known as 8900 Caroma Street. The CUP was reviewed for
a revocation and site expansion proposal in July 2025. (File # CU25-0004). 

APPLICATION SUMMARY
On October 10, 2019, a Conditional Use Permit was granted by the Board of 
(Zoning) Adjustment to allow a towing service and motor vehicle repair on the 2.94+/- 
acre property located on the north side of Caroma Street and west of HWY 305, known 
as 8900 Caroma Street, Olive Branch, MS, for a period of twenty years (20 years), 
subject to various conditions. The property is zoned C-2, Highway Commercial District. 
Approval Condition No. 5 stated that “CUP is issued to Carlos Murguia and Enrique 
Hernandez at the request of property owner Diane Hawks, Hawks Brank LLC, the 
property owner of 8900 Caroma Street. It is non-transferable to individuals other than 
Carlos Murguia and Enrique Hernandez or to a different property. Any expansion or 
alteration of the use is subject to BZA review and approval.” Approval Condition No. 6 
also stipulated that “A salvage yard is not permissible; outdoor storage of items 
including, but not necessarily limited to inoperable (other than those being repaired) and 
unlicensed vehicles, tires, vehicle parts, or scrap metal is strictly prohibited.” 
On July 10, 2025, the BZA reviewed two separate, but somewhat related items 
regarding the CUP: firstly, a violation of the above condition no.6 because the business 
owner was storing vehicle repair materials outdoor and a proposal by the property owner
to expand the site. Whie the BZA recognized that the business owner had made 
significant efforts in cleaning the property after the City served him notice of the CUP 
violation, the Board also considered that the site expansion improvements, although 
being a separate item, could provide a permanent solution to the outdoor storage of auto
repair materials because it included a new building addition. The BZA “approved the 
proposed expansion subject” to ten conditions. Approval Condition no.8 stipulated that 
“Final Set of civil site, landscape plans, elevations and a lighting plan shall be submitted 
for administrative review and approval received by July 9, 2026” and Condition No. 10 
stated that “The applicant shall complete the expansion by December 31, 2027. An 
updated status is required every 6 months by staff to BZA. The Planning Director or 
designee may extend this time for an additional six (6) months if the site is substantially 
expanded as depicted on the site plan by this date.” This report provides the required 
status update by staff to the BZA.
CURRENT STATUS
At the time of this report:
1.
The property and business owner has not yet submitted a final set of civil, 
landscaping, building elevations, and lighting plans for the expansion to the 
City. The property owner, Mr. Henry Hernandez, still has till July 9, 2026, to 
do so. However, he has stated to staff that current interest rate remains high. 
As such, he is reconsidering whether to pursue the site expansion.
2.
As shown in the attached site pictures, Mr. Hernandez is putting up a 
temporary screen as shown below around the auto-parking area to the 

Page 4 of 5
southeast front of the property. The screen consists of metal panels, which he
has painted black.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Director, Venard Asongayi, presented the staff report, which is included herein by
reference (File # CU25-0004).

BOARD OF ZONING ADUSTMENT INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
Mr. Roman asked on the Caroma Street side whether it was gravel or paved. Mr. Asongayi
advised it is paved. Mr. Williams asked if they would consider this again in July. Mr. Asongayi said
that we could, or if there is a compliance issue, we can bring back before that for revocation. He
advised the applicant agrees with all the new conditions by the July 2026 deadline.

PUBLIC HEARING
o
Proponents:

Luis Hernandez, 8900 Caroma Street, Olive Branch, MS
o
Opponents:

None

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
Mr. Roman said city and applicant are all in agreement. Mr. Gray says this is going to be easier
to complete and quicker. Mrs. Butler said interest rates have not been favorable. 

MOTION
Mr.Graymadeamotion,toapprovethattheConditionalUsePermitforanAuto-RepairShop
at 8900 Caroma St is hereby re-validated subject to the following:
1.
All parking and loading stalls/areas must be maintained off-street and be striped to
such dimensions as required in the Zoning Ordinance. 
2.
Maintain designated ADA access aisle and ADA parking space on the property.
3.
Any signage shall comply with the requirements of the Sign Ordinance.
4.
All cars on the property parked outside of the screened area must be parked in
stripped stalls.
5.
Thereshallbenooutdoorstorageofmaterials,includingbutnotlimitedtojunkmetal,
vehicle parts, and other such materials associated with the conduct of the business.
6.
Future expansion of the business shall require reconsideration of the Conditional
Use Permit, irrespective of the 20-year validity (till October 10, 2039) of current
approval.
7.
No later than July 1, 2026, the property owner shall screen only the east side of the
chain-link-fenced vehicle parking area with the 6ft high dark material being used
currently for concealment of the area.
8.
No later than July 1, 2026, the property owner shall remove the dark material being
currently used for concealment of the front and west side of the chain-link-fenced
vehicles parking area, and replace it with a 6ft high composite fence having an
impermeable cap. The gate into this area shall also have full-screen composite
material. 
9.
Stagger evergreen shrubs between existing shrubs in front of the current chain-
link-fenced vehicles parking area and add at least two of such evergreen shrubs to
the west of the dumpster enclosure. The evergreen shrubs shall be at least 5ft tall at
the time of planting.

Page 5 of 5
10. There shall be a mandatory annual review of the conditions of the property,
especially regarding compliance with Conditions 1 to 9 above to foster public health,
safety, and general welfare
Mr. Williams made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Absent Carl Williams- Yes
2.
General Policy Discussion:
Mr. Asongayi wanted to notify the Board that the Mayor had wanted to discuss how long
the Board of Zoning Adjustment gives applicants to make requested improvements. He
believes that sometimes less time may be appropriate. Auto repair shops, in general, are
becoming more and more non-compliant with Code Enforcement. When a Conditional
Use Permit is approved for 20 years, there can be constant issues with compliance. The
hope is that if the approval window is shortened to 5 years, but made renewable, the
applicant feels more compelled to maintain compliance. We have a new system in place
to provide build in alerts to bring forward for review. If you consider limiting auto repair
shops in this manner, we can incorporate into the Zoning Ordinance update. Mr. Roman
said it seems like a good practice to limit them. He acknowledged there have been issues
in the past and he gets that interest rates aren’t where we would like them. Ms. Wiseman
says this might put some pressure on the applicant to maintain their property, rather than
buying time to continue without any real progress. Mr. Williams said that 5 years seems
like a short time frame for this process to go through. He asked if it could be triggered a
Code Violation, for instance, maybe 10 years, with 5-year renewal if there are violations.
Mr. Asongayi said that the Zoning Ordinance can always change and might change within
that time frame. For example, in 2019, there was no screening requirement. 5 years gives
an option to enforce new changes to the code to maintain design elements and property
upkeep. Mr. Williams said there are a lot of auto shops that don’t comply. 
Mr. Roman mentioned the one across from City Hall and asked if it was due to come up
for review. Mr. Asongayi said it will be coming up for review in April. He advised that
Kevin was working on with the owners and providing landscaping advice. The problem
has been identified.
If there is no resolution by April, we will be coming back with a
revocation. We can’t force them to irrigate, just plant and maintain life.
Mr. Asongayi
also suggested they may want to request a minimum lot size for auto repair shops to
ensure there is enough room, possibly 2.5 acres. That suggested was approved and Mr.
Asongayi said that could be introduced as an update to the Code.
ADJOURNMENT
Mrs. Butler made a motion to adjourn the meeting at 6:49pm.
Mr. Gray made the second
and the motion was approved as follows: 
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Absent Carl Williams – Yes

records.text:
MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH PLANNING COMMISSION
REGULAR MEETING MARCH 10, 2026
The Olive Branch Planning Commission meeting was held on Tuesday, March 10, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Dorr, Chairman of Planning Commission, at 6:00 p.m.
ROLL CALL
Janice Lewis, Dion Jones, Diane Senger, Pat Dorr, Donny Singh, Steve Stratton and Mark Long
were present, and a quorum was established. Venard Asongayi, Director, Kevin Norman, Senior
Planner, Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, and Heather James, Planning Technician, 
were present from the Planning and Development Department. 
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE FEBRUARY 10, 2026 MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the
February 10, 2026 meeting. Ms. Senger made a motion to approve the minutes as presented.
Mr. Long made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Yes Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
CONSENT AGENDA
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
Mr. Dorr announced New Business # 1 and noted that there was a request to table until April
14, 2026. 
1.
Consideration of an application to amend the Project Text for Trinity Park Planned
Development, submitted by Almotasem Nasser, on behalf of Moheeb Nasser, property
owner. The 16.21+/-acre subject property is zoned PUD, Planned Unit Development, and is
located at the southwest corner of Hwy 305 and Church Rd E, known as 8961 Church Rd.
The request is to add Medical Cannabis as a permitted use within Area 7 of the PUD. (File
# PD-26-0001). (Applicant requests table to April 14, 2026).

MOTION
Mr. Jones made a motion to table the item until April 14, 2026. Mr. Long made the second
and the motion to table the item was approved as follows: 
Pat Dorr - Yes Steve Stratton - Yes Donny Singh - Yes Dion Jones - Yes
 Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes

Mr. Dorr announced New Business # 4 and noted that there was a request to table until April
14, 2026. Since it was requested to be tabled, he would take that one out of order to go ahead
and finish the item.
4.
Consideration of an application for a Zoning Map Amendment, submitted by Michel Lebel,
Allen & Hoshall, on behalf of property owner Desoto County School District. The request is
to rezone 42.5+/-acres from PUD, Planned Unit Development, to A-R, Agricultural-
Residential District. The property owner intends to use the site for a Career Tech Center for
the Desoto County School System. The subject property is located on the east side of Craft
Rd, in the southeast corner of the future expansion of W Sandidge Rd and Craft Rd. (File #
RZN-26-0001). (Applicant requests table to April 14, 2026).

MOTION
Mr. Jones made a motion to table the item until April 14, 2026. Mrs. Lewis made the second
and the motion to table the item was approved as follows: 
Pat Dorr - Yes
Steve Stratton - Yes
Donny Singh - Yes
Dion Jones - Yes
Janice Lewis -Yes Mark Long - Yes Diane Senger - Yes
2.
Consideration of an application for a revised Preliminary Plat for Carson Creek, submitted by
Greg Russell, Civil Source, on behalf of property owner, Marion Threat, Woolsey Road
Group.
The request is to create 25 single-family residential lots from 38.6+/-acres.
The
subject property is zoned R-1, Single-Family Residential District, and is located on the east
side of Davidson Rd, just over 400 feet north of Tranquil Dr. (File #SD-26-0004).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Greg Russell submits for consideration a preliminary plat for the Carson Creek Subdivision
on the subject property. The proposed single-family residential development will include 25
buildable single family detached lots and two common areas designated for stormwater
management.
The ±38.62-acre vacant property is currently zoned R-1 (Single-Family
Residential), which requires a minimum lot size of 12,500 square feet. The Board of
Aldermen voted unanimously (7–0) at its October 21, 2021 meeting to rezone the property
to R-1, Single-Family Residential. The smallest proposed lot is 1.00 acre. The developer shall
extend public utilities to service each lot.
The developer proposes the construction of new internal streets with a single access point
from Davidson Road, a street stub for future connection to Bending Elm Street in the northerly
Asbury Place subdivision, and no interconnectivity to the southerly Country Place subdivision
or the easterly Country View estate lots subdivision.
The plat meets both Zoning and
Subdivision Regulations.
Staff recommends approval of the preliminary plat, subject to
multiple conditions.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, presented the staff report, which is included
herein by reference (File # SD-26-0004).

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
 Mr. Long wanted to see sidewalks, and said that the neighborhoods all around 
this location have sidewalks. Mr. McCroskey said that Country Place and Country View 
do not have them and they are directly adjacent. Mr. Long said that future development 

may have smaller lots and will have sidewalks. Mr. Jones said if the smallest lot was 1 
acre, and still requiring garage not facing the street, whether or not the developer had 
any issues. They have no issues at all. Mr. Russell said the land cost and the building 
costs have been driven up so high, but relative to all the other costs. There is not 
enough profit margin in any other size lots. He is trying to keep development costs down
as much as possible to keep overall costs lower. Mr. Jones asked if these houses be 
similar to each other or will they all be custom. Mr. Russell said they are not the builder, 
these will all be sold, so he doesn’t know how they will build out.

PUBLIC MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone was present to speak for the application but advised that no
public hearing was required for a plat application.
o
Proponents:

Greg Russell, 2696 Dogwood Circle, Southaven, MS – he said the 
crossings over the creek are very expensive and larger lots decreased 
infrastructure costs. It’s difficult to put sidewalk next to a roadside ditch
of larger lots. The road that stubs out to the triangular area is not a 
developable lot. He said they agree with all conditions.
o
Opponents:

None

PLANNING COMMISISON DISCUSSION
Mr. Asongayi said the tendency has been to go from larger lots to smaller, but the
reverse can also be true. Larger lots have greater value with city amenities, but have “country-
like” lots, and they are usually higher value lots. These lots are usually individually built by the
owners on their own. Sidewalks are not required when 1 acre lots are approved for the entire
development. The density is low enough that people can walk safely on the street itself. 

MOTION
Mr. Jones made a motion to approve the revised preliminary plat for Carson Creek
Subdivision and recommend same to the Board of Aldermen subject to the following: 
1.
Improvements shall be the responsibility of the developer and not the 
responsibility of the City of Olive Branch.
2.
Grading, drainage, and civil construction plans to be approved by the City 
Engineer.
3.
The developer shall install drainage pipe, erosion control material, sewer 
mains and service, water mains, fire hydrants, gravel or soil cement base, 
and asphalt for all streets, with the thickness and layering to be determined 
by the City Engineer. A letter of credit, in an amount set by the City 
Engineer, must be filed prior to recording the plat to ensure the completion 
of all uncompleted public improvements prior to issuance of any building 
permit for any lot on the property.
4.
Plans for landscaping and entry feature/signage in common open space 
areas subject to review and approval of City Planning & Development 
Director, or designee. 
5.
For Final Plat submittal, the draft Declaration of Covenants Conditions & 
Restrictions will need to be customized for the Carson Creek 
Subdivision. The Declaration language should include the intent to impose a
2,000 heated sq. ft. minimum house size and design requirements for 

minimum 2/3 brick (or masonry) on all sides, uniform mailboxes, and 
requirements that garage doors will not face the public street. 
6.
Street light plans to be submitted to the City Engineer for approval.
7.
Street identification and traffic control signs and devices to be installed by 
the developer to City specifications.
8.
All utilities and services (electric, telephone, cable, etc.) to be installed 
underground. The water service lines shall be installed with tracing wire at 
the top.
9.
The development construction plans shall satisfy all other requirements as 
may be deemed necessary by the City Engineer to promote public safety, 
health and general welfare.
Mr. Singh made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr Yes Steve Stratton Yes Donny Singh Yes Dion Jones Yes
Janice Lewis Yes Mark Long Yes Diane Senger Yes
3.
Consideration of an application for the 2nd Revision to Lots 12 & 13, Craft Rd Industrial Park
Subdivision, submitted by Mike Davis, The Reaves Firm, on behalf of property owner SM
Lawrence. The request is to combine the existing Lot 12 and 13 and create a single Lot 12A
of 1.38+/-acres. The subject property is zoned C-2, Highway Commercial District, and is
located on the northwest side of Industrial Dr approximately 840 feet west of Old Craft Rd,
known as Lot 12, Craft Road Industrial Park, 8211 Industrial DR. (File # SD-26-0003).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Mike Davis RLA, The Reaves Firm, on behalf of KCKM Properties, LLC, property
owner, requests approval of the “Final Plat for Craft Road Industrial Park Subdivision, 2nd
Revision to Lots 12 & 13”. This is a minor plat revision that seeks to replat Lots 12 and 13 by
removing the lot line between the two lots and combining them. Public utilities such as gas,
water, and sewer are readily available to the proposed Lot 12A, which would be accessed
from Industrial Dr. The suggested plat revision meets requirements of the Zoning Ordinance
and the Subdivision Regulations of the City of Olive Branch. Staff recommends approval
subject to various conditions. 

STAFF PRESENTATION
Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, presented the staff report, which is included herein
by reference (File # SD-26-0003).

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None

PUBLIC MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone was present to speak for the application but advised that no
public hearing was required for a plat application.
o
Proponents:

Mike Davis, Reaves Firm, 6800 Poplar Ave, Memphis, TN– he had 
nothing to add to the 
o
Opponents:

None


PLANNING COMMISISON DISCUSSION
None

MOTION
Mr. Jones made a motion to approve the “Final Plat for Craft Road Industrial Park 
Subdivision, 2nd Revision to Lots 12 & 13”, subject to the following conditions:
1.
Lot improvements shall be the responsibility of the developer and not the 
City of Olive Branch.
2.
Reflect the two (2) sanitary sewer manholes and sewer line on the plat near 
the Southeast property line of original lot 13
3.
Add 20’ easement (10 feet on each side of sewer) along above-mentioned 
sewer line
4.
Remove 15’ proposed sewer easement along the northwest property line of
original Lot 13, unless otherwise determined as needed by the City 
Engineer.
5.
Future development on Lot 12A shall comply with all requirements of the 
City’s various land development regulations.
6.
Unless otherwise specified, all new utilities and services (electric, 
telephone, cable, etc.) shall be installed underground. The water service 
lines should be installed with tracing wire at the top.
7.
Minor edits are applicable to the final plat as may be required by City 
regulations and deemed necessary by City staff.
Mr. Stratton made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr Yes Steve Stratton Yes Donny Singh Yes Dion Jones Yes
Janice Lewis Yes Mark Long Yes Diane Senger Yes
OTHER BUSINESS
1.
Zoning Ordinance Updates
Mr. Jones had emailed suggestions to Asong, and they are being kept as part of the record. Some
of the ideas are already included in the proposed changes and some are new. There are a lot of
sound planning ideas in the documents. We just have to look at them in context with our area. An
example would be setting aside a specific conservation area, but where would we put it. These are
some ideas to think about. 
Overlay districts are proposed in the updated Ordinance documents.
For example, overlaying
existing zoning districts to meet certain additional requirements, but only within the confines of that
overlay. Examples would be the commercially zoned property along Goodman, but overlaying the
area from the edge of the road back 200 feet and everything that falls under that to have specific
additional signage requirements. But it would not affect the rest of the Commercially zoned property;
only what falls within that 200 feet.
PUD’s that are 40 acres and above in size, (Dove’s Landing, Wealth Hospitality, Oak Park Town
Center, for example) are different from PUD’s that are smaller.
It’s harder to apply the same

standards across the board. We may need to develop regulations specific to the smaller scale mixed
use areas. 
Mr. Asongayi proposes that the members take the documents home and study them. Next month,
there will be maps for everyone to see what is already in place and what may be able to be
introduced. The maps should be color-coded to what already exists and what has potential.
Regarding the Old Towne proposals, visit Old Towne and think about the suggestions and what can
be implemented. The majority of ideas are implemented in traditional downtowns. The Old Towne
Design Review Committee will meet later in March to discuss these suggestions. 
Updated maps for the entire city will be coming out in July to match the proposed changes to the
Zoning Ordinance. We can plan on some lengthier discussions as it gets closer to the submittal for
approval. 
Mr. Singh mentioned that Crumpler Place Apartments checked all the required boxes for the criteria
for zoning, but was still denied by the Board of Aldermen. Mr. Asongayi said that rezoning criteria
came into play on that project because they had requested a change to the uses allowed by the
Project Text. 
Mr. Dorr said we will study these and during the April meetings, we can discuss further.
ADJOURNMENT
Mr. Jones made a motion to adjourn the meeting at 6:50 pm.
Ms. Senger made the second
and the motion was approved as follows: 
Pat Dorr Yes Steve Stratton Yes Donny Singh Yes Dion Jones Yes
Janice Lewis Yes Mark Long Yes Diane Senger Yes

MINUTE SUMMARY 
 1 
MARCH 3, 2026 

BE IT REMEMBERED that the Mayor and Board of Aldermen of the 
City of Olive Branch met in regular session, March 3, 2026 at 6:00 
o’clock p.m., in the Municipal Court Room at 6900 Highland Street. 

AGENDA 
 
Mayor Adams called the regular meeting to order at 6:00 
o’clock p.m. 

INVOCATION: 
 
George Black, Rejoice Church had the opening prayer. Mayor 
Adams led the Pledge of Allegiance. 

ROLL CALL (Establish Quorum): 
 
The City Clerk called roll to establish quorum with the 
following members present to wit: Mayor Kenneth R. Adams, 
Alderwoman Jan Aldridge, Alderman George Collins, Alderman Dale 
Dickerson, Alderman Gil Earhart, Alderman Don Gammage, Alderwoman 
Pat Hamilson, and Alderman David Wallace. These members constitute 
a quorum. Also present were Tena Stewart, City Clerk and Bryan 
Dye, City Attorney. 

APPROVAL OF MINUTES: 
 
Minutes of the Regular Meeting held February 17 2026, approved 
as presented, motion carried unanimously. 

ANNOUNCEMENTS: 
 
Mayor Adams shared a written overview of the City’s website 
with the Board of Aldermen and highlighted information regarding 
usage. 

CONSENT AGENDA: 
 
Items on Consent Agenda approved as presented, motion carried 
unanimously. Consent Agenda items as follows: 
 
1. Travel/Training Approved 
 
2. Appoint Kelsey Roach as deputy clerk for the purpose of 
receiving and distributing funds and attending training. 
Appointed 
 
3. Authorize the City of Olive Branch to renew annual rental 
agreements with Premier Air Products and pay all associated 
costs. Authorized 
 
4. Authorize the City of Olive Branch to renew the annual 
subscription with Solvit, Inc. and pay all associated costs. 
Authorized 

 MINUTE SUMMARY 
 2 
MARCH 3, 2026 

5. Approve membership for Police Captain Terri Hoskins to FBI 
LEEDA and pay all associated costs. Approved

records.text:
Page 1 of 4
 MINUTES FOR THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT
REGULAR MEETING FEBRUARY 12, 2026
The Olive Branch Board of Adjustment meeting was held on Thursday, February 12, 2026, in the
Municipal Court Room located at 6900 Highland Street, at 6:00 p.m.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mr. Roman, Chairman of Board of Zoning Adjustment, at 
6:00 p.m. 
ROLL CALL
Ted Roman, William Gray, Aretha Wiseman, Darrel Berkley, Jackie Butler and Carl Williams were
present, and a quorum was established. McKeever Heun was absent. Venard Asongayi, Director,
Jeremiah McCroskey, Associate Planner, Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, and Heather James,
Planning Technician, were present from the Planning and Development Department.
THE APPEAL PROCESS
Mr. Roman announced the Appeal Process.
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES OF THE DECEMBER 11, 2025 MEETING
Mr. Roman asked if anyone had any questions, comments or motions regarding the minutes of the
December 11, 2025 meeting. Carl Williams made a motion to approve the minutes. William Gray
made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Yes Carl Williams – Yes
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
1.
Application for a Zoning Variance, submitted by Nicholas Nanos, property owner. The request is to
permit a 25-foot encroachment into the 50-foot front setback in order to install a 6ft high privacy
fence. The1.46+/-acresubjectpropertyiszonedA-R,Agricultural-ResidentialDistrict,andislocated
at the northeast corner of Hummingbird Dr and Bluebird Ln, known as 7790 Hummingbird Dr. (File
# VR-26-0001).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
The property owner, Nicholas Nanos, requests a variance to allow construction of
a six-foot-high privacy fence within the required fifty-foot front yard setback. The 
proposed fence would be located twenty-five (25) feet from the front property line. Article
VII, Section 2(B)(c)(ii)(A) of the Zoning Ordinance limits fences within the front yard to a 
maximum height of three (3) feet. Accordingly, the applicant seeks both a twenty-five-
foot front yard encroachment variance and a +3 ft fence height variance for the a six-
foot-high fence.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Associate Planner, Jeremiah McCroskey, presented the staff report, which is
included herein by reference (File # VR-26-0001).

Page 2 of 4

BOARD OF ZONING ADUSTMENT INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None

PUBLIC HEARING
o
Proponents:

Nicholas Nanos, 7790 Hummingbird, Olive Branch, MS – He had nothing to add,
but he will be thankful as this will protect the vision of his bedroom and kitchen
windows.
o
Opponents:

None

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
None

MOTION
Mr. Williams made a motion, based on finding that a hardship exists and all the criteria have
been met, to approve the request to permit a 25 ft. encroachment into the 50-foot front setback in
order to install a 6 ft high privacy fence on the property located at the northeast corner of
Hummingbird Dr and Bluebird Ln, known as 7790 Hummingbird Dr.
Mr. Berkley made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Yes Carl Williams – Yes
2.
Application for a Conditional Use Permit, submitted by Darius Totten, on behalf of property owner,
Bobby Depriest. The request is to establish an auto repair shop at 8749 MWC Rd for a period of 2
years. The 0.68+/-acre subject property is zoned C-2, Highway Commercial District, and is located
on the west side of MWC Rd, approximately 330 feet from the end of the road. (File # CU-26-0001).

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Darius Totten, on behalf of A Team Auto Repair and Bobby DePriest, property 
owner, requests approval of a conditional use permit for 2 years for an automotive repair
shop at 8749 MWC Rd, upon Lot 17, Mineral Wells Commercial Subdivision. The 
applicant has requested only a 2-year CUP as the automotive repair business is 
planning to move to a different location in the future. The existing 0.68 ac subject 
property is on the west side of MWC Rd, approximately 675 ft south of the intersection of
US Hwy 178 and MWC Rd. The applicant submitted an existing conditions site sketch 
that shows an aerial view of the site consisting of a ±6,098 sf building, a ±4,000 sf front 
parking lot, and a ±19,500 sf fenced-in area. There is an existing wrought iron gate and 
fencing toward the front of the repair area, with chain-link fencing surrounding the 
remainder of the repair area. A landscape plan has not been submitted, however the 
applicant has agreed to install screening, install landscaping, and remove cars under 
repair to behind an opaque screen.

STAFF PRESENTATION
Senior Planner, Kevin Norman, presented the staff report, which is included herein
by reference (File # CU-26-0001).

Page 3 of 4

BOARD OF ZONING ADUSTMENT INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
Mr. Roman asked how long this auto shop had been in existence and asked if there was a
prior Conditional Use Permit. Mr. Norman advised there was not one, but this application was to
bring him into compliance with the ordinance. 

PUBLIC HEARING
o
Proponents:

Darius Totten, 8749 MWC Rd, Olive Branch, MS – He advised he’s been there a
little over a year. 
o
Opponents:

Steve Cooksey, 8708 MWC Rd, Olive Branch, MS – he said he had 2 questions
about this project. He said this was originally set up as a commercial property, not
to handle the larger 18 wheelers. Is this planning to be for heavy trucks or smaller
passenger vehicles. His second question, regarding parking on the street, wa s
addressed by the presentation. 

BOARD OF ZONING ADJUSTMENT DISCUSSION
Mr. Roman asked Mr. Totten if he was planning on moving to a new location in the future and if
that’s why it was only be asked for 2 years. Mr. Totten advised that was correct. This is a temporary
location. Mr. Norman advised that this shop will not be handling the larger 18 wheelers, but regular
passenger vehicles. Mr. Totten confirmed that he would not be working on any heavy trucks. Mr.
Asongayi advised that the Board can add a condition stating that the repair of 18 wheelers is
prohibited. 

MOTION
Mr. Williams made a motion, based on the Board of Adjustment’s finding that all
requirements have been met, to approve a Conditional Use Permit for an automotive repair shop at
8749 MWC Rd, upon Lot 17, Mineral Wells Commercial Subdivision, for a period of 2 years subject
to the following conditions:
1.
All cars stored outdoors must be fully screened in length, width, and height by the
applicant from view from MWC Rd by February 28, 2026. The gate should also be
treated with an opaque screen and should remain closed when not in active use to
access the parking area at the side and rear of the building. Outdoor storage of
vehicular materials and junk cars is prohibited.
2.
Remove existing dead crape myrtles and provide 2
3-inch to 3.5-inch perimeter
landscape trees along MWC Rd and 1 2-inch to 2.5-inch medium interior parking tree
within the existing raised island to comply with Section 36-75 Landscaping Ordinance.
3.
Any future expansion of the development would require approval by the Board of
Adjustment.
4.
All materials and fluids stored on-site must meet requirements of the Fire Code.
5.
Relocate all cars under repair from the parking area along MWC Rd to behind the
opaque screen.
6.
All cars parked in front of the building must be in striped parking spaces at all times.
7.
Parking on the MWC Rd right-of-way is strictly prohibited.
8.
Auto repair approval does not cover diesel or heavy truck repair.

Page 4 of 4
Mr. Gray made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley
OTHER BUSINESS
ADJOURNMENT
Mr. Gray made a motion to adjourn the meeting at 6:23pm. Ms. Wiseman made the second
and the motion was approved as follows: 
William Gray – Yes McKeever Heun - Absent Aretha Wiseman – Yes
Ted Roman – Yes Jackie Butler – Yes Darrel Berkley – Yes Carl Williams – Yes

Consideration of an application for the 1st Revision of Acree Planned Commercial
Subdivision, Phase 3, submitted by Harvey Matheny, The Pickering Firm, on behalf of
Mohammed Said, David & Sons, LLC, property owner. The request is to replat Lot 9 and Lot
10 to 1.06+/-acres and 1.3+/-acres, respectively. The subject property is zoned C-4, Planned
Commercial District, and is located at the northeast corner of Jericho Way and James Herbert
Dr. (File # SD-26-0001).
Mr. Stratton arrived at 6:03PM, during the presentation for New Business Item 1.

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Harvey Matheny, The Pickering Firm, on behalf of Mohammed Said, David & Sons, 
LLC, property owner, requests approval of the Final Plat for the 1st Revision of Acree 
Planned Commercial Subdivision, Phase 3. This is a minor plat revision that seeks to replat 
lots 9 and 10 by moving the lot line between the two lots eastward. Public utilities such as 
water and sewer are readily available to both lots. Access to Lot 10 would be from Jericho 
Way and to Lot 9 would be via a cross-access easement over lot 10 as currently recorded. 
The suggested plat revision meets all requirements of the Acree Planned Commercial 
Development project text and the Subdivision Regulations of the City of Olive Branch. Staff 
recommends approval subject to various conditions.


STAFF PRESENTATION
Venard Asongayi, Director, presented the staff report, which is included herein by
reference (File # SD-26-0001). He noted the correction to Condition #4 regarding the sign
easement needing to be maintained by the owner of Lot 13.


None


public hearing was required for a plat application.
o
Proponents:

Harvey Matheny, Pickering Firm, 6363 Poplar Ave, Ste 300, Memphis, 
TN– he had nothing to add to the report and noted the appreciation for 
staff making the correction regarding the maintenance agreement.
o
Opponents:

None

PLANNING COMMISISON DISCUSSION
None

MOTION
Ms. Senger made a motion to approve the Final Plat for the “1st Revision of Acree 
Planned Commercial Development, Phase 3” subject to the following conditions:
1.
Lot improvements shall be the responsibility of the developer and not the 
City of Olive Branch.
2.
Future development on the lot shall comply with all requirements of the 
City’s various land development regulations.
3.
Unless otherwise specified, all utilities and services (electric, telephone, 
cable, etc.) shall be installed underground. The water service lines should
be installed with tracing wire at the top.
4.
Restate the following note on the proposed plat: “The Acree Commercial 
Sign in the Sign Easement on Lot 10 shall be constructed and maintained 
by the owner of Lot 13. The sign shall be monument style, no more than 
12 feet in height, and no more than 100 square feet in size. Business 
names advertisement on this sign shall be restricted to the businesses on
the lots lying south of James Herbert Drive, between C.O.S. C19 and 
C.O.S. A16 as shown on the final plat for Acree Planned Commercial 
Development Subdivision, Phase 3, recorded in Plat Book 154, Page 46.”
5.
Minor edits are applicable to the final plat as may be required by City 
regulations and deemed necessary by City staff.
Mrs. Lewis made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr Yes Steve Stratton Yes Donny Singh Yes Dion Jones Yes
Janice Lewis Yes Mark Long Yes Diane Senger Yes

2.
Consideration of an application for the Final Plat of Sullivan Minor Subdivision, submitted by
Jordan Bledsoe, Bledsoe Engineering and Surveying, on behalf of Bonnie Sullivan, property
owner. The request is to create 3 detached single-family residential lots totaling 4.95+/-acres.
The subject property is zoned A-R, Agricultural-Residential District and is located on the
south side of Pleasant Hill Rd, approximately 470 feet west of the intersection of Balterson
Loop and Pleasant Hill Rd, known as 4529 Pleasant Hill Rd. (File # SD-26-0002). 

APPLICATION SUMMARY
Jordan Bledsoe, Bledsoe Engineering & Surveying LLC, on behalf of property owner,
Bonnie Sullivan, requests approval of the final plat for Sullivan Minor Subdivision, which will
consist of 3 detached single-family residential lots. The parent parcel to be subdivided is
currently zoned AR, Agricultural Residential district. The AR zoning district requires that all
lots be a minimum of 1 ac in area. A 2-inch gas line and 6-inch water main run within both
the Pleasant Hill Rd N right-of-way and Summers Creek right-of-way. Existing fire hydrants
are located at the end of Summers Creek Rd and along Pleasant Hill Rd N. Lot 1 would
maintain access from Pleasant Hill Rd, while Lots 2 and 3 would be accessed through a
shared easement from Summers Creek Rd. Staff recommends approval subject to various
conditions. 

STAFF PRESENTATION
Kevin Norman, Senior Planner, presented the staff report, which is included herein
by reference (File # SD-26-0002).

PLANNING COMMISSION INQUIRY AND STAFF RESPONSE
None

PUBLIC MEETING
Mr. Dorr asked if anyone was present to speak for the application but advised that no
public hearing was required for a plat application.
o
Proponents:

Jordan Bledsoe, 5717 Jason Cove, Olive Branch, MS – he had nothing
to add to the report.
o
Opponents:

None


Mr. Jones had a question for staff. He asked if the connection to Summers Creek Drive
wide enough for 2 separate driveways to access separately, rather than a shared easement. Mr.
Asongayi advised normally, there would be allowed 50 feet per lot for access. Mr. Jones asked
if the cul-de-sac was too small to allow this and Mr. Asongayi advised it was, and that was why
the easement.
Mrs. Lewis asked about the process for septic set up through the Health
Department. She asked how long that took and at what point in the process that was set up. Mr.
Asongayi said that it’s handled after the plat is recorded and the building permit is obtained. Mrs.
Lewis asked if it was difficult to get that handled and Mr. Asongayi advised that it was not.

MOTION
Mr. Jones made a motion to approve the final plat for Sullivan Minor Subdivision and
recommend same to the Board of Aldermen subject to the following: 

1.
The Final Plat shall be recorded before any new construction upon Lots 1, 2,
and 3.

Improvements shall be the responsibility of the developer and not the
responsibility of the City of Olive Branch.

A common paved driveway shall be installed within the perpetual common
access easement to service Lots 2 and 3. 
4.
Individual septic tanks may be used in subdivisions where central sewage is
not available only if written approval is obtained from the Desoto County
Health Department.
Mrs. Lewis made the second and the motion was approved as follows:
Pat Dorr Yes Steve Stratton Yes Donny Singh Yes Dion Jones Yes
Janice Lewis Yes Mark Long Yes Diane Senger Yes

FEBRUARY 17, 2026

records.text:
MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING OF THE MAYOR 
 1 
AND BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH 
FEBRUARY 3, 2026 

BE IT REMEMBERED that the Mayor and Board of Aldermen of the 
City of Olive Branch met in regular session, February 3, 2026 at 
6:00 o’clock p.m., in the Municipal Court Room at 6900 Highland 
Street. 
 
AGENDA 
 
Mayor Adams called the regular meeting to order at 6:00 
o’clock p.m. 

Alderman Gil Earhart had the opening prayer. Mayor Adams 
led the Pledge of Allegiance. 

ROLL CALL (Establish Quorum): 
 
The City Clerk called roll to establish quorum with the 
following members present to wit: Mayor Kenneth R. Adams, 
Alderwoman Jan Aldridge, Alderman George Collins, Alderman Dale 
Dickerson, Alderman Gil Earhart, Alderman Don Gammage, Alderwoman 
Pat Hamilton, and Alderman David Wallace. These members constitute 
a quorum. Also present were Tena Stewart, City Clerk and Bryan 
Dye, City Attorney. 

APPROVAL OF MINUTES: 
 
Minutes of the Regular Meeting held January 20, 2026, approved 
as presented, motion carried unanimously. 

PUBLIC COMMENTS: 

Mr. Joe Ricker, Coach for the Desoto Technix Robotics along 
with three (3) team members Nathan, Team Captain, Bella and Raymond 
attended and addressed the Board sharing recent events and 
requested financial support for upcoming travel. The Desoto 
Technix Robotics team is comprised of seven (7) community based 
high school - homeschool students. Coach Ricker shared the team 
won the State of MS Championship and was 1 of 2 Mississippi Teams 
to advance to the World Championship. The World Championship, 
representing fifty-six (56) countries, was held in Houston, TX. 
The Desoto Technix Robotics placed 4th in their division and ranked 
7th out of 8,000 teams. The team was also selected by Governor 
Tate Reeves to represent the State of Mississippi in the first 
annual Governor’s cup. 

ANNOUNCEMENTS: 
 
Mayor Adams and the Board of Aldermen presented Park Operator 
Eddie Baldwin and Park Groundskeeper Taylor Swallers with a 
privately-funded monetary recognition of exceptional dedication 
and service and for demonstrating initiative, selflessness and a 
strong work ethic daily. 
 
Mayor Adams congratulated Alderman Don Gammage and Police 
Chief Carlos Garcia for receiving Trail Blazer Awards. 
 
Mayor Adams gave a brief review of Municipal status and 
responses related to the recent ice storm. Mayor Adams noted that 

 MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING OF THE MAYOR 
 2 
AND BOARD OF ALDERMEN OF THE CITY OF OLIVE BRANCH 
FEBRUARY 3, 2026 

although the Olive Branch Airport was closed to private aircraft, 
FEMA and TVA were able to utilize the airport to bring helicopters 
in and out for emergency response during the ice storm. 
 
CONSENT AGENDA: 
 
Items on Consent Agenda approved as presented, motion carried 
unanimously. Consent Agenda items as follows: 
 
1. Travel/Training Approved 
 
2. Appoint Joshua Mucciarone as deputy clerk for the purpose of 
receiving and distributing funds and attending training. 
Appointed

MINUTE SUMMARY 
 1 
JANUARY 20, 2026 

BE IT REMEMBERED that the Mayor and Board of Aldermen of the 
City of Olive Branch met in regular session, January 20, 2026 at 
6:00 o’clock p.m., in the Municipal Court Room at 6900 Highland 
Street. 
 
AGENDA 
 
Mayor Adams called the regular meeting to order at 6:00 
o’clock p.m. 

Paul Bryant, Cross Creek Church had the opening prayer. 
Mayor Adams led the Pledge of Allegiance. 

ROLL CALL (Establish Quorum): 
 
The City Clerk called roll to establish quorum with the 
following members present to wit: Mayor Kenneth R. Adams, 
Alderwoman Jan Aldridge, Alderman George Collins, Alderman Dale 
Dickerson, Alderman Gil Earhart, Alderman Don Gammage, Alderwoman 
Pat Hamilton, and Alderman David Wallace. These members constitute 
a quorum. Also present were Tena Stewart, City Clerk and Bryan 
Dye, City Attorney. 

APPROVAL OF MINUTES: 
 
Minutes of the Regular Meeting held January 6, 2026, approved 
as presented, motion carried with Alderwoman Aldridge, Alderman 
Collins, Alderman Dickerson, Alderman Earhart, Alderman Gammage 
and Alderman Wallace voting in favor, and with Alderwoman Hamilton 
abstaining. 

ANNOUNCEMENTS: 
 
Mayor Ken Adams, the Board of Aldermen and Fire Chief William 
Clark recognized members of Engine 1 and Unit 1 who in September 
of 2025 responded to an emergency call at City Hall involving an 
unresponsive individual. These individuals were instrumental in 
sustaining life during a critical medical emergency and reflect 
the highest standards of public service and exemplify the 
dedication and commitment of the Olive Branch Fire and EMS 
Department. Receiving the Lifesaving Award: Fire Lt./EMT Jeff 
Hawks, Driver/Paramedic Patrick Depriest, FF/EMT Will Preslar, 
FF/EMT Jaiden Bell, Paramedic Peyton Elkins, and Paramedic Paul 
Coletta. 
 
Mayor Adams recognized Mr. Noah Melugin from Scout Troop 097 
who was in attendance at the meeting. 
 
Mayor Adams recognized 2 members of the Mayor’s Youth Council 
who were in attendance at the meeting. 

CONSENT AGENDA: 
 
Items on Consent Agenda approved as presented, motion carried 
unanimously. Consent Agenda items as follows: 

 MINUTE SUMMARY 
 2 
JANUARY 20, 2026 

1. Travel/Training Approved

12 place setting of chinaware and drinking glasses from Dianna 
Crumpler to be displayed at the Wesson House. Authorized

receiving and distributing funds and attending training.

Grant Application to the U.S. Department of Justice. Approved

for the Olive Branch Animal Control Department. Authorized

Section 25-1-47 - 7095 Apache Drive. Approved
